If you want to get back together, first work out what you truly want. If you're together, keeping some time alone each can actually be better. Set aside a quiet stretch and write down what you truly want in this relationship.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, don't apply at random yet. Think through your long-term direction. In collaboration, it helps to organize your own thoughts before you talk. A current project needs time to settle and deeper study. Set aside some quiet time and write down how you really feel about your work right now.
upright.ask_next: If no one else had a say, what would your own answer be?

reversed.overall: The Hermit reversed means the strength of solitude has gone off course. You may have shut yourself away for too long and lost touch with the world. Or you may be staying busy to avoid stopping and thinking about a problem. The lamp is still in your hand. Now you need to decide: go out more and reconnect with people, or sit down quietly, once, and face the question you keep avoiding.
reversed.love: If things are undefined, one of you may have closed off, and the other feels pushed away. If you've lost contact, tell the difference between truly missing them and just not wanting to be alone. If you want to get back together, don't rush back out of fear of loneliness. If you're together, one of you has been hiding in their own world for too long. Once you're clear in your mind, send a simple greeting first.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you've been avoiding thinking about your direction. In collaboration, you're used to carrying everything yourself and won't ask for help. On your current project, you're working in silence and feeling more alone the further you go. Talk with someone you trust about where you are, and let their lamp light up what you can't see yourself.
reversed.ask_next: Right now, do you need more time alone to think it through, or someone to talk to?

upright.overall: At the center of the card is a large wheel, and in the four corners winged figures sit on clouds reading books while the wheel keeps turning. This card says things are moving. What was stuck is starting to loosen, and some factors outside your control are turning your way. It's better now to adjust along with the change than to hold hard to your original plan.
upright.love: In love, this card often appears when a relationship is shifting: someone you're unsure about suddenly responds, someone you lost contact with reappears, a new opening comes up for getting back together, or a couple's rhythm changes. Don't rush to call it good or bad. Notice what's different this time compared with before, then decide whether to take a step forward.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, a new opening or invitation may appear. In collaboration, the situation has changed, so the terms can be renegotiated. If your project's direction has changed, clinging to the original plan will cost you. Update your résumé and portfolio now, so you can respond right away when an opportunity shows up.
upright.ask_next: What do you want to know: whether this change is worth keeping up with, or whether you should steady yourself first?

reversed.overall: The wheel is upside down. It's still turning, but you feel you keep circling back to the same place. Reversed, this card doesn't mean your luck is getting worse. It means the same pattern keeps showing up, or you've hit the brakes in the face of change. Look back: how many times have you met a situation like this? The spot where you're stuck is often where you haven't changed your approach.
reversed.love: Whether things are undefined, you've lost contact, or you're trying to get back together, the two of you may be going around the same loop: cold for a while, hot for a while. If you're together, you argue about the same thing every time. Rather than wait for the other person to change, find the point where you get stuck each time, and try saying or doing it differently next time.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, your effort doesn't seem to be bringing change. In collaboration, the same problem keeps coming up. On your current project, you know it needs adjusting but haven't acted. Write down the things that went wrong recently and look for what they share. That is often where you need a new method.
reversed.ask_next: Are you stuck because of outside conditions, or because you keep handling it the same way?

upright.overall: The figure on the card holds a sword in one hand and scales in the other, looking straight at you. This card is about laying things out and seeing them clearly: who did what, and who is responsible for what. What you're getting now is mostly tied to earlier choices. It's a good time to separate facts from feelings and judge more calmly. If something needs you to take a position, see it clearly first, then act.
upright.love: If things have been undefined for a long time, check whether what you give and what you get back are equal. If you've lost contact, honestly review what each of you did back then. If you want to get back together, first talk through what each of you is responsible for. If you're together, look at whether the division of effort and giving is fair. Say plainly what matters to you, and listen to how the other person answers.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, bring specific numbers and results when you negotiate terms. In collaboration, write down roles and responsibilities clearly. On your current project, your performance will be noticed, but your own part needs to be done completely. For important documents and agreements, read them line by line before replying.
upright.ask_next: What do you want to clarify in this matter: the other person's responsibility, or your own choice?

reversed.overall: The scales are upside down. You feel things aren't quite fair, or your judgment is being pulled off by emotion. Reversed doesn't mean you'll lose out. It reminds you that what you see now may be only part of the picture. Don't rush to a conclusion. Gather more information, or hear from someone who takes no side. When your mood settles, look at the matter again.
reversed.love: If things are undefined, it may be that you alone have been the one giving way. If you've lost contact, each of you feels more wronged than the other. If you want to get back together, dredging up old grievances will only tilt the scales further. If you're together, one of you has been putting up with things. Don't keep score. Start with one small recent thing and say clearly how you want to be treated.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you may be wavering back and forth on one decision. In collaboration, the workload is uneven. On your current project, the evaluation feels unfair. Write out what happened, and talk with evidence in hand. If needed, ask your manager to help sort out who does what.
reversed.ask_next: The unfairness you feel: is it something you can say out loud, or something you've kept inside?

upright.overall: The figure hangs upside down from a tree, yet looks calm, with a ring of light behind the head. This card is about a pause: things can't be pushed forward right now, and forcing them won't help. But the time you spend stopped can show you angles you normally can't see. It's a good moment to let go of wanting a result right away and think in a different direction. The answer won't arrive just because you're in a hurry.
upright.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, the relationship is hanging with no progress. If you're out of contact, the other person hasn't given an answer yet, and pressing them usually doesn't help. If you want to get back together, try standing in their position and think about what's worrying them. If you're together, it's a good time to stop arguing over who's right. Bring your attention back to yourself first, and give each other some space.
upright.work: If you're job hunting, you may still be waiting to hear back. If you want to change jobs, an offer or promotion keeps being delayed. A collaboration may be stuck on the other side, and a project you're running can't move for now. Use this time to learn a new skill, or to rethink what position you really want.
upright.ask_next: Right now, are you waiting for the other person, or for yourself to get clear?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the Hanged Man means not stopping when you should, or stopping so long that it becomes a habit. You may be putting a lot into something without being sure it's worth it. Or you keep saying "let's wait a bit more" when you really don't want to make a decision. This card reminds you that waiting needs a purpose, or it's just dragging things out. Ask yourself first: if the answer never comes, what will you do?
reversed.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, you keep waiting for the other person to state their feelings until you're worn out. If you're out of contact, "let's wait a bit more" may really mean not wanting to face it. If you want to get back together, you've given way a lot without getting a response. If you're together, the other person may not see your sacrifice. Set yourself a boundary: if there's no response, it's your turn to move forward.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you keep telling yourself to put up with it a little longer. In collaborations, you may be sacrificing too much for the other side. A project you're running is dragging with no conclusion. Write down clearly what you're waiting for: a raise, a transfer, or courage? Once it's on paper, it's easier to tell whether to keep waiting.
reversed.ask_next: For the thing you're waiting for, is there a line at which you'd be willing to let go?

upright.overall: A knight in armor rides a white horse, and in the distance a sun rises between two towers. This card isn't about something bad but about an ending: a stage has reached its close, and old patterns or old forms of a relationship need to be put away to make room for the new. It's a good time to admit that "this chapter is over." Letting go isn't easy, but it's the start of moving forward.
upright.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, you may need to move from vague to clear, or simply let go. If you're out of contact, this silence may itself be a kind of closing. If you want to get back together, the old way of relating has to end first for something new to be possible. If you're together, some habit needs replacing. Write down what you want to hold on to: the person, or that period of time.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, an old stage of your career is coming to a close. A working relationship may be near its end. A project or a way of working is about to be put away. Rather than struggling on, hand things over well and wrap up well. A clean ending lets you put your whole self into the next step.
upright.ask_next: What you really want to end: is it the thing itself, or your expectations of it?

reversed.overall: Reversed, this card means something that should end is still dragging on. You may know in your heart that a stage has passed but don't want to let go yet, so things hang there and nothing new can come in. This isn't a bad omen, just a slower change. Start by closing off one small thing, and loosen your grip little by little. Going slowly is fine. What matters is that you're moving forward.
reversed.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, the relationship stays unclear and neither of you will say it out loud. If you're out of contact, you keep checking their updates. If you want to get back together, what you miss may be the past, not who they are now. If you're together, no one mentions the parts that are already hollow. Take one small action, like putting away your chat history, to give yourself some room.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you may be staying in a position you know doesn't fit just because it's familiar. A collaboration has long since stopped working but no one calls it off. A project you're running drags on without being closed. List your reasons for staying, and see how many you truly want and how many are just fear of change.
reversed.ask_next: The reason you won't let go: is it that you still hope, or that you fear the emptiness afterward?

upright.overall: The angel has one foot in the water and one on the shore, slowly pouring water back and forth between two cups. This card is about mixing and balance: things don't need to be right all at once, but adjusted bit by bit in proportion. It's a good time to slow down, find the middle, and bring different needs together. Rushing for a result makes it easier to spill the water.
upright.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, there's no need to rush to define the relationship. If you're out of contact, you can start by restoring a little interaction in a light way. If you want to get back together, gradually adjusting how you relate is steadier than one big showdown. If you're together, talk about where your paces differ. Take one topic at a time and align slowly.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, it's a good time to find a middle ground between ideal and reality. In collaborations and cross-team work, you may be the one coordinating in the middle. A project you're running needs resources brought together. Before acting, ask each side for their bottom line, then find an approach everyone can accept.
upright.ask_next: What you want to adjust in this situation: is it the other person's pace, or your own expectations?

reversed.overall: When the water pours unevenly, one side may have too much and the other too little. Reversed means the proportions have slipped: doing too much, asking too much, or rushing to see results. This isn't failure, just a need to retune the rhythm. First find which part you're pushing too hard, and spread that effort back out. Doing a bit less and giving yourself room to breathe often gets you back on track faster.
reversed.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, one side is warm and the other cold. If you're out of contact, you can't help sending more and more messages. If you want to get back together, you're giving so much the other person can't take it in. If you're together, your paces are starting to mismatch. Stop and ask what distance feels comfortable to them, instead of adding more.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you may be applying to too many places at once and can't keep up. In collaborations, the two sides' rhythms don't match. On a project, you've taken on too much and packed it too full. Set priorities for your work and let go of one or two things that aren't urgent. When you can't keep up, ask your manager directly to help you set the order.
reversed.ask_next: Where you feel out of balance: are you giving too much, or expecting too fast?

upright.overall: On the card, two people are chained to a pedestal. Look closely and you'll see the chains around their necks are actually quite loose. This card is about being tied to something: a habit, a relationship you can't let go of, or a fixed idea about how things should turn out. It reminds you that, often, you are holding the key yourself. Start by seeing clearly what is holding you, and you'll know where to begin untying it.
upright.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, you may be caught in a strong attraction with no commitment. If you're no longer in contact, you may keep checking their profile. If you want to get back together, you may keep returning even though you know it isn't a good fit. If you're together, you may rely too much on the other person's responses. Write down whether this relationship makes you feel more at ease or more anxious. Your honest answer is the clue.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you may be tied down by salary, title, or habit. In a collaboration, one side may be locked in by the terms. A project may be wearing you out, yet you can't stop. Write down what you would need in order to leave or adjust, such as how much to save or how much time it takes, and the chain won't feel as heavy.
upright.ask_next: Is it this person or this thing you can't let go of, or the feeling you've gotten used to?

reversed.overall: The reversed Devil is the start of noticing you're bound and wanting to take the chains off. You may already see that a habit or relationship is draining you, and you are slowly loosening your grip. This may not be quick, and you may look back now and then, but you're moving toward freedom. Be patient with yourself. Each time you choose to take care of yourself, the chain loosens a little more.
reversed.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, you can finally say, "I don't want this anymore." If you're no longer in contact, you're learning to stop opening their page again and again. If you want to get back together, watch for a single remark from them that could pull you back. If you're together, you're beginning to ease off an overly dependent pattern. Tell a friend you trust about your decision so you have support.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you're starting to think about leaving a job that drains you. In a collaboration, you're beginning to see which terms have tied you down. In a project, you want to change a habit of procrastinating or overworking. Start with one small change, such as leaving work at a set time, and feel what it's like to be loosened.
reversed.ask_next: What you want to loosen, is it an outside condition or a habit inside you?

upright.overall: On the card, lightning strikes a tower, the crown at its top is blown off, and two people fall from it. This card is about sudden change: something you thought was solid cracks, or something is suddenly revealed. It's jarring, but it also lets you see a problem you hadn't noticed and gives you a chance to rebuild. Steady yourself first, then decide where to start rebuilding.
upright.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, a fact may come out and the relationship changes suddenly. If you're no longer in contact, one direct clash may open up what was stuck. If you want to get back together, your original picture may be broken. If you're together, built-up problems may rise to the surface all at once. Don't rush into big decisions. Let your emotions settle, then talk it through properly.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, your plan may be thrown off. A collaboration may suddenly stop or change terms. A project may be hit by an organizational shift. Deal with what must be handled right now, then take stock of the resources you still have and confirm the new priorities with your manager.
upright.ask_next: With this change, do you most want to understand the cause first, or what you can do next?

reversed.overall: The reversed Tower means a change that's due is delayed, or that you keep propping up something that already has cracks. You may sense something is off but not want to face it yet. This doesn't mean it will get worse. It's a reminder that dealing with it on your own initiative is easier than waiting for it to fall. You can start by looking clearly at the smallest, most avoided piece. Things are often not as hard as you imagine.
reversed.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, you're both pretending nothing is wrong. If you're no longer in contact, some things have never been said openly. If you want to get back together, the old problems are still there, just covered up. If you're together, small cracks keep piling up. Talking early is easier than letting it build until it bursts. Start by raising one smaller thing.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you already feel the company isn't stable but are still waiting and watching. In a collaboration, there's a problem no one mentions. In a project, you're holding up a plan that has cracks. Prepare a backup, such as organizing your portfolio or contacting former colleagues, so you have options.
reversed.ask_next: What's behind your not wanting to face the thing you keep holding up and avoiding?

upright.overall: On the card, a woman kneels by the water and pours from two jars onto the pool and the land, with one large star and seven small stars in the sky. This card appears after turmoil and means slow recovery and a renewed sense of direction. Things won't get better all at once, but you can start to trust that step by step it will become clearer.
upright.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, you can express more of your true self. If you're no longer in contact, take care of yourself first, and once you feel steady, decide whether to reach out. If you want to get back together, speak up again with a calm, sincere attitude. If you're together, there's less guardedness between you. Find a quiet moment and tell them something from the heart.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, it's a good time to reset your goals and send out applications. In a collaboration, sincerity is your best calling card. A project may not pay off right away, but the direction is right. Write down the outcome you want, then break it into small steps you can do, and build up slowly.
upright.ask_next: What do you most want to regain right now: confidence in this relationship, or in yourself?

reversed.overall: With the reversed Star, the water is still pouring, but for now you can't see the starlight. You may be tired, a little discouraged about what you hoped for, and wondering if it's still worth sticking with. The hope hasn't disappeared. You need to rest first, regain a little strength, and then look at your direction again. Sleeping enough or talking with a friend are ways of helping yourself find the light again.
reversed.love: If you're in an ambiguous situation, you've waited a long time with no response and are starting to wonder if you're overthinking. If you're no longer in contact, your hopes keep falling through. If you want to get back together, don't draw conclusions from a moment of disappointment. If you're together, being with them is wearing you out a bit. Bring your attention back to your own life, let your mood settle, then decide whether to keep waiting.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting, you've sent many applications and heard nothing. If you want to change jobs, you've lost confidence in the direction. In a collaboration, your enthusiasm has been worn down. In a project, you've run out of energy. Pause and ask yourself why you wanted to do this in the first place. Find that reason again, then keep going.
reversed.ask_next: Is what discourages you that the result hasn't come yet, or that you've started doubting this direction?

upright.overall: On the card, the moon hangs between two towers. Below, a dog and a wolf howl at it, and a crayfish crawls out of the water. This card is about not being able to see clearly: the information is incomplete, and imagination and worry are easily magnified. It's not a good time to rush to a judgment. First separate what is fact from what is your guess. Your intuition is worth listening to, but check it against evidence.
upright.love: If you're in a situationship, the other person runs hot and cold and you keep rereading their messages. If you've lost contact, the less you hear, the more your mind fills in the blanks. If you want to get back together, longing and worry are mixed up together. If you're together, there may be an unease you can't put into words. Guess less and check directly more. Simply asking one question is enough.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you may still have doubts about an offer. In collaboration, the other side's intentions aren't clear. A project you're on isn't transparent. List what you're unsure about as questions and ask them one by one. Until you have concrete answers, don't make any decision you might regret.
upright.ask_next: What's unsettling you: facts you know, or possibilities you've imagined?

reversed.overall: With the moon reversed, the fog is starting to lift. Something that has been bothering you may be getting answers, or you may be realizing that many of your worries were you scaring yourself. This is a good time to sort things out: which doubts have been settled, and which still need checking. The little path to the distance on the card is becoming easier to see. Once the answers come, take care of your feelings first, then decide what to do.
reversed.love: If you're in a situationship, you finally hear what the other person really feels. If you've lost contact, you find that many of your worries were self-made. If you want to get back together, you see clearly why you parted. If you're together, a misunderstanding is slowly clearing up. Even if the answer isn't what you hoped for, it's better than guessing. Take time to absorb it, then decide whether to move closer or keep your distance.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you understand what a position is really like. In collaboration, the other side's position is finally stated clearly. The direction of a project you're on is becoming clear. Put the information into writing now, as a basis for your next decisions, and if you have questions, ask them now.
reversed.ask_next: Does what you can see clearly now change the decision you were planning to make?

upright.overall: On the card, a child rides a white horse, with a field of sunflowers behind and a bright sun overhead. This card stands for clarity, openness and energy: things are in the sunlight and there's nothing to hide. Right now it suits you to speak up and show who you are, and your effort is more likely to be noticed. While you're in good form, take one step forward on something you want to do.
upright.love: If you're in a situationship, you can openly show that you like them. If you've lost contact, a relaxed, friendly hello is enough. If you want to get back together, say honestly what you think, without circling around it. If you're together, do something fun together. You don't need clever lines. Just say what you feel, sincerely.
upright.work: If you're job hunting, it's a good time to interview and show what you can do. If you want to change jobs, your strengths are easy to notice. The team mood is good, so it suits pitching ideas. A project you're on is ready to show results. Turn your recent results into concrete numbers or examples and let your manager or interviewer know.
upright.ask_next: What do you want the other person to know: how you feel, or what you need?

reversed.overall: With the sun reversed, the light is still there, just slightly covered by cloud. Things are generally heading in a good direction, but may be slower than expected, or you may be tired and unable to find your enthusiasm for now. You may also be too optimistic and missing some details. This card reminds you to recharge first, then fill in the details. Good things are still on the way. They just need a little more patience and adjustment.
reversed.love: If you're in a situationship, the warmth seems to have cooled a little. If you've lost contact, the response you hoped for is coming later than you imagined. If you want to get back together, you may be picturing it as better than it was. If you're together, some freshness has faded. Don't write off the whole relationship because of a moment of coolness. Plan a date that's different from usual.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, good news may come a little later. In collaboration, you're too optimistic about results and missing risks. A project you're on is moving slower than expected. Go back and check the details, patch the places that could go wrong, and sync with your team on progress.
reversed.ask_next: What feels missing: a response from outside, or your own enthusiasm?

upright.overall: On the card, an angel blows a trumpet, and people below rise from their coffins with arms open to the sky. This card is about a moment of waking up: you finally see what this situation really looks like, and you know how you want to respond. Past experience isn't a burden but the basis for doing better this time. It's a good time to look back honestly, then make a decision you're willing to take responsibility for.
upright.love: If you're in a situationship, you'll be clearer about what you want. If you've lost contact, you may get a chance to think things over again. If you want to get back together, the point isn't whether to turn back, but whether you've worked out the original problem. If you're together, it's a good time to look at the relationship afresh. Write down your thoughts, then decide whether to speak.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you may get an opportunity that makes you rethink your direction. In collaboration, an old partner may show up again. On a project you're on, you suddenly understand what your manager cares about. Summarize your years of experience on one page, and see clearly what you're good at before you negotiate.
upright.ask_next: Is the decision you want to make now for yourself, or for other people's expectations?

reversed.overall: The trumpet has sounded, but you haven't stood up yet. Judgement reversed isn't bad news. It means you're too hard on yourself, or still doubting whether you deserve to change. You may keep replaying where you went wrong and end up stuck in place. This card reminds you that reviewing the past is for moving forward, not for punishing yourself. Go a little easier on yourself first, and the answer will be clearer.
reversed.love: If you're in a situationship, the more you think, the less you dare to move. If you've lost contact, you keep scrolling through old messages. If you want to get back together, you can't help judging yourself for what went wrong. If you're together, you easily read too much into a single remark. Stop scrolling through old messages and ask yourself: setting fear aside, what do you really want?
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you have an opportunity but feel you're not good enough yet. In collaboration, you dwell on past mistakes. On a project you're on, you're afraid of being wrong and can't make a decision. Ask a trusted colleague to tell you what you do well, and use their eyes to recalibrate your own.
reversed.ask_next: Is what keeps you from deciding the fear of choosing wrong, or the fear of what others will think?

upright.overall: A dancer stands inside an oval wreath, with an angel, an eagle, a lion, and an ox in the four corners. This is the last card of the Major Arcana, and it marks a road reaching its complete end. What you've worked on is being harvested, and the different parts of your life are slowly lining up. It's a good time to wrap things up properly, acknowledge yourself, and carry what you've learned into the next stage.
upright.love: If things are undefined, it may be time to say clearly what this is between you. If you're no longer in contact, the relationship may have run its course, and you can let it go well. If you want to get back together, first check that you've truly worked out the lesson of the last round. If you're together, the relationship is reaching a mature, steady place. Pick a relaxed moment and say what the two of you are like now.
upright.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you've learned what this position had to teach you. A collaboration is reaching a smooth close, and your current project is entering its final stage. Finish the work properly first, then put together a record of your results. It will help whether you're asking for a raise or changing careers.
upright.ask_next: For you, is this chapter truly complete, or do you just want it over quickly?

reversed.overall: The world is upside down. The wreath is still there, but the circle hasn't quite closed. This isn't failure. It means you're one step short: a few details may be unhandled, or part of you may not want this stage to end. Without a finish, the next step can't begin. List what's still undone, close each item one by one, and give yourself a real full stop.
reversed.love: If things are undefined, the relationship is stuck right at the edge of being made clear. If you're no longer in contact, a relationship that never ended well is still on your mind. If you want to get back together, there's still something you haven't said. If you're together, you keep putting off talking about the next step. First work out which sentence is stuck, then decide whether to say a proper goodbye or talk about the future.
reversed.work: If you're job hunting or changing jobs, you want to leave but haven't formally said so. A collaboration is stuck at the final wrap-up, and your project is dragging at the end with the handover unfinished. Break the remaining work into a list and start with the easiest item to close, so things get moving again.
reversed.ask_next: What you keep leaving unfinished: is it the task itself, or the feeling you can't bear to lose?

upright.overall: A hand reaches out from a cloud holding a cup filled to overflowing. Five streams of water fall into a pond of water lilies below, and a white dove descends toward the cup with a wafer in its beak. The Ace of Cups is the beginning of a new feeling: a flutter of attraction, being moved, or fresh enthusiasm for something. It's pure, and you only need to receive it. There's no rush to define what it will become.
upright.love: This is a sign that your heart is starting to stir. If things are undefined, the other person's interest may be more real than you think. If you haven't been in contact for a while, the care in your heart is still there. If you want to get back together or you're already together, it's a good time to say your feelings out loud. Send a straightforward message and simply say what you truly feel right now.
upright.work: At work, you may truly feel something for a new project or direction, and that enthusiasm deserves to be taken seriously. When an invitation comes, first ask yourself whether doing this would make you happy. Write down the parts of work that move you. Later, when you look for jobs or discuss a role, you'll know which way to go.
upright.ask_next: What do you want to confirm: the other person's feelings, or whether your own heart is stirred?

reversed.overall: The card is upside down. The hand in the cloud and the overflowing cup are still there, but the flow has turned inward. Reversed, the Ace of Cups often means feelings are being hidden: you hold back what you want to say, or you're used to putting others first and your own needs last. It isn't that there's no love. The cup needs to turn toward you first. Work out what you want, then think about giving.
reversed.love: You have feelings, but you may be pretending not to care because you're afraid of being hurt. Leaving messages unanswered while things are undefined, picking up your phone and putting it down after a breakup, going back and forth before reconciling, or being together but unable to say it aloud are all this state. You don't need to force a response. Write down what you truly feel for yourself, and speak once you're sure.
reversed.work: At work, you may have lost enthusiasm for your current job and just get tasks done each day. Or you may be giving a lot without being seen. Find one small thing at work that still gives you a sense of achievement, put your energy back there, and slowly regain your drive.
reversed.ask_next: What do you need most right now: the other person's response, or your own rest?

upright.overall: A man and a woman face each other, raising their cups. Above them is a staff wrapped by two snakes, topped with a winged lion's head. The Two of Cups is about a connection that runs both ways: seeing each other and responding to each other. It isn't limited to romance and may be a collaboration or friendship. The key is "mutual." What you give has a chance of being received well.
upright.love: Both sides are willing to move closer. If things are undefined, the other person's response may be more serious than you think. If you're no longer in contact or want to get back together, this card leans toward there still being room for conversation. If you're together, it's a good time to compare your paces. Speak as an equal, without testing or deliberately going cold, and honestly say that you like them.
upright.work: It's a good time to discuss collaboration, look for partners, or smooth out communication with your manager. The other side is also looking for someone to work with. When negotiating terms, lay both sides' needs on the table and find an approach that works for both. It will last longer and stand firmer than one side always giving way.
upright.ask_next: What do you want to know: whether the other person feels the same, or how this can move forward?

reversed.overall: Turned upside down, the two people still hold their cups, but the balance between them has slipped. Reversed, the Two of Cups often means one person is giving more, or each assumes the other understands when nothing has really been said. The relationship isn't over. It needs adjusting. Instead of guessing, stop and check what each of you really thinks, then adjust together.
reversed.love: It might be read receipts with no reply or slower answers while things are undefined, a silence after no contact where neither wants to speak first, or being together while feeling you always give in. If you want to get back together, first look at whether the old gap was ever dealt with. Pick a calm moment and start with "I feel," skip the old arguments, and talk only about how you want to be together from here.
reversed.work: At work, a partnership may have mismatched expectations, such as unclear roles, or you and your manager picturing the result differently. Write each side's responsibilities and deadlines as a simple list and ask the other person to confirm it once. That prevents later misunderstandings better than relying on an unspoken understanding.
reversed.ask_next: What feels unbalanced to you: how much each of you gives, or the way you talk to each other?

upright.overall: Three women stand in a circle in a harvest field, raising their cups high, with ripe fruit at their feet. The Three of Cups stands for support and joy between people: friends, companions, those working together. You don't have to carry this alone. People around you are glad to share good news and willing to help. It's a good time to open up your social circle, talk with people you trust, and celebrate what you've achieved at this stage.
upright.love: This card often relates to your circle of friends. If you're single or in an undefined romance, you may grow closer through gatherings or mutual friends. If you're out of contact, you may hear news of the other person through friends. If you're together, it's a good time to be seen together among each other's friends. Plan a relaxed get-together with friends there and let the relationship breathe.
upright.work: Teamwork is going well, or there is a result worth celebrating, and good relationships with colleagues will help you now. Thank the people who worked with you, or organize a small get-together to bring the team closer. Moving things forward will go much more smoothly afterward, and you'll have people to consult when problems come up.
upright.ask_next: In this matter, do you want your friends' opinions, or just someone to keep you company?

reversed.overall: The three women still hold their cups high, but turned upside down, the celebration has gone a bit too far. Reversed, the Three of Cups means too much social energy spent: too many gatherings, too many obligations, or small frictions and gossip in the circle. You may also feel left out. It's a reminder to return to your own pace and choose the people you truly want to spend time on.
reversed.love: Too many people giving opinions may be confusing you more: friends teasing you about an undefined romance, asking around about someone after no contact, or talk of getting back together being discussed in a group chat. If you're together, friends' affairs may also affect how you get along. Keep the two of you's business between the two of you, meet alone first, and listen to what each really thinks.
reversed.work: The team mood may be a bit delicate, with private cliques or messages passed along, or too many dinners and social obligations may be getting in the way of real work. Stay out of talk behind people's backs, speak directly to the person involved if there's a problem, and put your energy back into your own results.
reversed.ask_next: Right now, do you need more company, or some quiet time?

upright: Missing what's in front of you

upright.overall: A young man sits under a tree with his arms crossed. Three cups sit on the ground in front of him, and a hand from a cloud offers a fourth, which he seems not to notice. The Four of Cups is a kind of weariness: no interest in what you have, and no energy to look at new possibilities. Rest and reflection are needed. Just don't let this impatience block the opportunity in front of you as well.
upright.love: You may find the current interaction dull and feel little for someone who is showing interest. After no contact, you may not bother to reach out again, or be half-hearted about reconciling while still thinking of other possibilities. If you're together, you may be taking the other person's effort for granted. List three things they've done for you lately. Some kinds of care aren't expressed through grand gestures.
upright.work: At work, you may be tired of your current job and uninterested in new offers. When you're worn out, it's easy to miss a good opportunity. Don't rush to refuse. Ask for the details first, give yourself some time to think, and then decide whether to take it.
upright.ask_next: Is it that this isn't right for you, or that you're simply too tired?

reversed.overall: Turned upside down, the young man under the tree and the hand offering the cup are both still there, and this time he has a chance to turn his head. Reversed, the Four of Cups mostly means you are slowly coming out of weariness and becoming willing to accept something new. Another reading is that you pull back even further and shut yourself in. Which one applies depends on where you are now. Ask yourself honestly: am I resting, or avoiding?
reversed.love: You may be starting to respond to feelings you had ignored: you finally want to answer that message in an undefined romance, someone you've lost contact with comes back to mind, or you resist reconciling less. If you're together, you may be interested in how you relate again. If you still want to be alone, that's fine. Simply saying "I need some space lately" is much better than not replying at all.
reversed.work: At work, after a period of stagnation, you're starting to want to move. That might mean sending out your résumé again or approaching your manager about a new task. Start with one small thing, like answering the email you've been putting off or signing up for a class, and get yourself moving again step by step.
reversed.ask_next: What do you want to seize right now: this opportunity in front of you, or a chance to catch your breath first?

upright.overall: A figure in a black cloak looks down at three cups that have fallen and spilled, while two intact cups still stand behind. In the distance, a bridge crosses a river. The Five of Cups is about the sadness that follows a loss. That feeling is real and deserves to be treated with care. But it also reminds you that not everything is gone: something remains, and there is still a path ahead.
upright.love: It might be a breakup, lost contact, a flirtation that faded out, or a relationship where your hopes weren't met, and you may keep wondering what you did wrong. If you want to get back together, look at what is still left, even through the sadness. Allow yourself to grieve, but don't fixate only on what's gone. Write down what you truly gained in this relationship, and see what you can take with you.
upright.work: At work, this might be an interview you didn't get, a proposal that didn't pass, or effort that didn't bring the return you expected. Disappointment is normal, but don't write yourself off entirely. Once you've calmed down, look back at what went well and write it down. You'll feel more confident next time.
upright.ask_next: What are you struggling most to let go of: that person or that thing, or the person you were back then?

reversed.overall: Turned upside down, the two cups standing behind the figure in the black cloak become easier to see. Reversed, the Five of Cups means you are slowly accepting the loss and starting to regain your strength. But if the regret is never dealt with, it can turn into a habit of looking back. You already have the ability to cross that bridge. What's left is deciding whether to take the first step.
reversed.love: You may be starting to let go of an ex, or be willing to talk through old hurts with someone you lost contact with. If you want to reconcile, you can also look at the original problems more calmly. If a flirtation let you down, you're slowly coming back to yourself. If you're together, you may finally be able to put old grudges aside. Give your feelings a concrete outlet, like clearing out some old belongings or replying to a message you've left unanswered.
reversed.work: At work, the earlier setback is passing and you're starting to want to try again. The biggest risk now is being afraid to try again because of one failure. Consider sending your résumé out again, or revising a rejected proposal and resubmitting it, so this experience becomes an advantage next time.
reversed.ask_next: Do you feel ready to move forward, or is there still something you want to finish saying?

upright: People and things from the past

upright.overall: One child hands a cup holding white flowers to a smaller child, and the cups around them are all in bloom, set in a quiet courtyard with an old house behind. The Six of Cups stands for memories and simple kindness: old friends, familiar places, or something that makes you feel safe. It's a good time to take a little warmth from the past, remember what you first loved, and meet what's in front of you with a softer heart.
upright.love: An old acquaintance may get back in touch, someone you lost contact with may send news, or warm memories of an ex may surface. If you're in a flirtation, talk about your childhoods and shared memories. If you're together, recall how you first met. Start in a light way, such as sharing an old photo, and find your natural ease again.
upright.work: At work, past contacts or experience may become useful again, such as a former coworker introducing an opportunity or an old skill being needed. Reach out to a few people you enjoyed working with and catch up. Sometimes opportunities are hidden in those old connections.
upright.ask_next: Who do you miss: that person, or yourself during that time?

reversed.overall: Turned upside down, the flowers are still in the child's hands, but it's as if you've been standing in that courtyard and never left. Reversed, the Six of Cups means being too attached to the past: you've made the memories prettier than they were and compare them with the present, so nothing now feels good enough. This isn't asking you to forget the past. You can treasure memories, but life has to be lived in the present.
reversed.love: You may keep thinking about an ex, or measure the people in your life now against past feelings. After losing contact, you may reread old conversations, or the other person wants to reconcile while the original problems are still there. In a flirtation, you may compare the person to an old love. If you're together, you may keep comparing the present with the early passionate days. First sort out whether you miss this person or the feeling of being cared for.
reversed.work: You may be used to doing things the old way, or keep missing your former team and adjust to the new environment more slowly. List three things you can learn in the new setting. Shifting your attention from comparing to your own growth will make things easier, and you'll be more likely to be noticed.
reversed.ask_next: If he came back, would things be different between you, or do you just want the familiar feeling back?

upright.overall: A figure with their back to us looks at seven cups floating in clouds, holding a castle, jewels, a laurel wreath, a dragon, a snake, and a covered, glowing figure. The Seven of Cups means there are many options, but most are still in the imagination. Each one is tempting, but not necessarily real. The point isn't to imagine one more possibility, but to tell which ones you truly want and can actually do.
upright.love: You may be drawn to several people at once, or have many imaginings about a flirtation or an ex you've lost contact with, without being sure what they're really like now. If you want to reconcile, you may be missing the version in your memory. If you're together, you may compare your partner with an ideal one. Write down what the other person has actually done lately, and get to know them through their actions.
upright.work: You may have several directions you want to try, or receive different offers at once, and not know how to choose. Make a table of each option's conditions, pay, commute, and room for growth, and lay them side by side. The answer usually becomes much clearer.
upright.ask_next: Among these options, which one do you truly want, and which one just sounds good?

reversed.overall: The mist is slowly clearing, and what's in the cups is easier to see. Reversed, the Seven of Cups means you're coming back from imagination to reality and know what you can let go of. It can also mean something else: so many options have worn you out that you'd rather not choose at all. This card suggests first cutting the two or three least realistic ones. With fewer choices, the decision comes more easily.
reversed.love: You may be starting to see the other person as they really are: the heat of a flirtation has cooled, your imaginings after lost contact have faded, or you have a more realistic view of reconciling. If you're together, you may accept your partner as they are. If you're still unsure, ask yourself: if you had to answer right now, who would you choose, or would you choose no one? Write that instinct down.
reversed.work: At work, you may finally decide to focus on one thing, or see that an opportunity isn't as good as you imagined. Tell your decision to someone you can talk it over with. Saying it aloud will make you more sure, and you may hear angles you hadn't considered, which can help you check whether you've missed anything.
reversed.ask_next: If you could keep only one option, which one would you cross off first right now?

reversed: Wanting to leave but afraid to

upright.overall: Under the moonlight, a figure with a staff walks toward distant mountains, back turned to eight stacked cups, with one gap left in the top row. The Eight of Cups is noticing that something no longer satisfies you, even though it still looks fairly complete. Leaving isn't failure. It's wanting a direction that fits you better. This is a good time to be honest about the emptiness you feel inside.
upright.love: If you're together, the relationship may feel like it's missing something, and you may want to pull back. If things are ambiguous or you've lost contact, you may decide to stop waiting for someone who doesn't respond. If you're hoping to get back together, you may find that what you want has changed. Figure out whether you want to leave this person or this way of being together. If it's the second, try having one real conversation first.
upright.work: Your current job may feel stable but empty, and you may be thinking about changing paths. That feeling deserves attention, but don't rush to resign. List what you want in a job, send out applications while you keep working, and leave once you have a direction. It's steadier, and you won't panic during a gap between jobs.
upright.ask_next: What do you want to leave: this person, this job, or the person you are right now?

reversed.overall: With the card upside down, the figure walking away from the cups hesitates. The reversed Eight of Cups is often wanting to go but not daring to, or knowing something doesn't suit you but fearing you'll have nothing after leaving. It can also mean you've already left but don't know where you're headed. This card doesn't push you to decide. It reminds you that staying or leaving should be your choice, not something fear pushes you into.
reversed.love: You may feel worn out in a relationship but stay out of habit. Maybe an ambiguous situation has dragged on and you can't bring yourself to end it, or you can't let go of an ex and swing between no contact and wanting to reconcile. Set aside some time alone to think quietly: if you weren't afraid of being lonely or of what others would say, what would you choose? Write the answer down.
reversed.work: You may have been saying you'll change jobs for a long time without acting, or you may have just left a job with no direction yet. Do one small thing that moves you forward, like updating your résumé or asking someone in the industry to talk. Turn the hesitation into a concrete next step you can actually take.
reversed.ask_next: Is what keeps you there something you still truly want, or just something you're used to?

upright.overall: A person sits on a wooden bench with arms crossed and a satisfied look, and behind them, nine cups line a curved, cloth-covered table. The Nine of Cups is often called the wish card. It means you've mostly gotten what you wanted, or you're close. It's a good time to admit your effort has paid off, enjoy it, and see clearly which part of this satisfies you. There's no need to rush toward the next goal.
upright.love: You feel mostly content in this relationship. If things are ambiguous, you may get the response you wanted. If you're waiting to hear from an ex, you may get an answer that puts you at ease. If you're together, you're in a comfortable stretch. Say out loud what you like, such as texting thanks for some small thing, so the other person knows what makes you happy.
upright.work: Things mostly go the way you hoped, perhaps you get the terms you wanted or a project goes out smoothly. Write down what you did right this time. Next time you negotiate or update your résumé, you'll have concrete results to point to, and your manager will see your contribution.
upright.ask_next: Right now, do you want to know whether this contentment will last, or what you need next?

reversed.overall: Upside down, the satisfaction of the person before the nine cups may stay on the surface: you got the thing, but it doesn't feel as solid as you imagined, or you fill the gap with food, drink and fun. This isn't asking you to deny yourself. It asks you to look back: what did you really want, and which piece is still missing? Once that's clear, the next step is easier.
reversed.love: You may have gotten the other person's attention and still feel it isn't enough. Maybe the chat is lively but goes nowhere, or a reconciliation after no contact only returns to a comfortable surface, or you're together and get along well but avoid deeper topics. Write down the one thing you truly want them to do, and think through how to bring it up. Be specific, and it will be easier for them to take in.
reversed.work: You may have gotten the terms you wanted but feel unmotivated, or your results are noticed and you still feel empty. Don't rush to change careers. List what satisfies you about this job and what doesn't, then decide whether to adjust or leave. You're less likely to regret that than an impulsive choice.
reversed.ask_next: Is what bothers you that you didn't get enough, or that what you got isn't what you wanted?

upright.overall: A rainbow arches across the sky with ten cups on it. Below, a couple embrace with arms raised, two children dance nearby, and a house stands in the distance. This card is about emotional belonging and fulfillment, a point where things feel secure and both people feel held. It's a good time to cherish the connections you already have.
upright.love: This card suits talking about the long term, and two people's pictures of shared life are fairly close. If you're together, talk about what each of you imagines as home. If things are ambiguous, watch how the other person treats the people around them. If you've lost contact or want to reconcile, consider whether you want the same kind of life. Turn vague expectations into one or two specific things.
upright.work: The team gets along well, or you find a place that gives you a sense of belonging. If you're comparing job offers, include workplace atmosphere and work-life balance as well as pay. Asking current employees how they feel can help a lot. See clearly before you decide, and you'll feel at ease with your choice.
upright.ask_next: Do you want to know whether this relationship can last, or whether you both want the same thing?

reversed.overall: Upside down, the rainbow and ten cups are still there, but a gap opens between the fulfillment in the picture and reality. Family or a partner may expect something you can't deliver, or everyone may look friendly while the real words go unsaid. The connection hasn't vanished. Someone just needs to put the truth on the table first, and after that you usually feel closer.
reversed.love: Your pictures of the future may differ, for example about living together or meeting family. If things are ambiguous, you may find you want different kinds of relationships. If you split up and want to try again, you may be stuck because your expectations of home don't match. Each say the one thing you care about most, then listen before responding. That helps more than guessing what the other thinks.
reversed.work: The team may look peaceful while people privately feel dissatisfied, or you may treat coworkers like family and feel let down when expectations aren't met. Spell out roles and boundaries, and communicate through concrete matters rather than relying on feelings alone. When expectations are spoken, there's less disappointment.
reversed.ask_next: Are you stuck because you want different things, or because no one has spoken first?

upright.overall: A young person in a patterned tunic stands by the sea. A small fish pops out of the cup in their hand, and they look at it with curiosity. This card stands for a new feeling or piece of news surfacing: a little flutter, a flash of inspiration, simple and curious. It isn't mature yet, but it's worth noticing. Don't rush to conclusions. Let it grow slowly.
upright.love: Often seen as a crush just beginning, or a message with a hint of testing from someone you're unsure about. A person you've lost contact with may also reappear with a small topic, and if you want to reconcile, it's fine to start with light interaction. For those together, a small surprise can bring freshness back. Share a song or a photo, and let each other get to know a little more first.
upright.work: There may be a new idea, a small invitation, or a chance to try something out. Write your idea up as a one-page draft and show it to your manager or partners. Testing it on a small scale is easier than starting with a big plan, and you'll find out sooner whether the direction is worth your effort.
upright.ask_next: Are you trying to confirm whether they mean it, or whether you want to respond?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the little fish is still in the cup, but the new feeling has been tucked away or overthought. You may have feelings you're afraid to voice, or you may be reacting to a small thing more strongly than usual. The emotion is real. It just needs to be expressed in a more mature way. Admit to yourself that you care, then decide how to say it.
reversed.love: The other person may be blowing hot and cold in their messages, or you keep rehearsing conversations in your head without speaking. If you're trying to win someone back after losing contact, you may be stuck on who should reach out first. For those together, a single remark can set you overthinking. Boil what you want to say down to one simple greeting and send it. Seeing how they respond will tell you more than guessing again and again.
reversed.work: You may have many ideas but none that land, or a single comment may affect your mood for days. Pick the most workable idea and write down the first step. When you receive criticism, first separate what is about the work from what is just your feelings, and your mood will be less likely to get dragged around.
reversed.ask_next: Are you waiting for the other person to speak up first, or are you willing to speak first yourself?

upright.overall: A knight in a winged helmet rides a white horse at a gentle pace, holding a cup out level in front of him as if offering it to someone. This card stands for an invitation or proposal made with heart, coming closer. The pace isn't fast, and it moves people through feeling and sincerity rather than pushing. You can take your time looking it over and responding.
upright.love: Someone may show interest, ask you out, or express themselves in a more romantic way. A person you've lost contact with may also come back with sincerity to talk about reconciling. For those together, a carefully planned date suits you. When you accept an invitation, watch whether what they say matches what they do, and when you meet, talk about each other's everyday lives, not just the mood.
upright.work: Someone may offer a collaboration or a job, with terms that sound very appealing. Ask them to put it in writing, including duties, pay, and timeline. Read the details carefully before replying, so the good feeling has something concrete behind it. If you have questions, ask them right away.
upright.ask_next: Do you want to know whether they're serious, or whether this invitation suits you?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the knight still holds the cup out, but the gesture is slow to arrive. Something promised may never be delivered, or someone may speak beautifully while their actions lag behind. It could also be that you've idealized something too much and need to look at it practically. Once you see clearly, the goodwill can still be offered well.
reversed.love: The person you're unsure about may be full of sweet talk but keep rescheduling plans. Someone you've lost contact with may say they want to reconcile while their actions don't follow. Or what you like may be the version of them in your imagination. For those together, you may have heard many promises with few kept. Suggest one concrete small plan, such as having a meal together, and see whether they actually show up.
reversed.work: An interview may have gone well but no news has followed, or a partner may promise a lot and then not move. Send a short message to confirm progress and next steps, and keep your other opportunities going. Whatever the outcome, you won't be left just waiting.
reversed.ask_next: Are you focused on what they say, or on what they actually do?

upright.overall: The Queen of Cups sits on a throne by the sea, holding an ornate lidded cup with angel handles in both hands, gazing at it intently. This card stands for delicate sensitivity and the ability to care for others. You can read the feelings people haven't said aloud. This is a good time to trust that intuition and handle things gently. Your feelings deserve to be trusted.
upright.love: You may be the one who understands the other person's feelings better. When it's unclear where you stand, you sense their hesitation, and after losing contact you can roughly tell where they're stuck. For those together or hoping to reconcile, this thoughtfulness is just what the relationship needs. When they talk, listen to the end first, then ask, "Do you need me to keep you company, or help you figure something out?"
upright.work: This suits tasks that involve communication, looking after clients, or coordinating a team, and your attentiveness will be noticed. Write up what you've observed for your manager so your intuition becomes concrete advice others can follow. Putting careful observation into words is your strength.
upright.ask_next: Right now, do you need more to look after them, or to look after your own feelings first?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the queen still holds the cup, but her attention may be entirely on others and she has forgotten herself. You may be absorbing too much of other people's emotions, or giving constantly without voicing your own needs. Gentleness needs boundaries too. Fill your own cup first, and you'll have energy left to care for others.
reversed.love: You may keep being understanding toward the other person while rarely voicing your own hurt. When it's unclear where you stand, you adjust yourself to their mood, and after losing contact one post from them can sway your whole day. If you're together or hoping to reconcile, notice whether you're the only one catching the emotions. In your next conversation, name one thing you need, such as "Even when you're busy, send me a quick reply."
reversed.work: You may often finish up colleagues' work, or your manager's mood may affect your whole day. Before agreeing, pause and say, "Let me check what's on my plate and get back to you." Save your time and energy for the work that is truly yours. Helping is fine, as long as you're willing.
reversed.ask_next: Are you tired from the work itself, or from constantly catching other people's emotions?

upright.overall: The King of Cups sits on a throne floating on rolling seas. A fish leaps from the water on one side, and a ship sails in the distance on the other. He holds a cup in one hand and a short scepter in the other, sitting steady. This card is about staying stable while emotions surge, facing things with a mature, tolerant attitude and not being carried off by a passing wave. This is a good time to be the one who steadies the situation: listen first, then speak.
upright.love: This is a relationship that needs stability and trust, and you or the other person is better able to carry the emotions. When it's unclear where you stand, you don't push for an answer, and when you've lost contact or are talking about reconciling, you can discuss it calmly. For those together, when friction comes up, you can wait for emotions to settle before talking. Try saying, "I'd like to talk this through properly. When is a good time for you?"
upright.work: Good for situations that call for a calm head, like handling a customer complaint, leading a team, or talking with your manager. Under pressure, write down the facts and your feelings separately, then decide how to respond. People see you as steady and reliable, and they feel more at ease handing things over to you.
upright.ask_next: What do you want to ask: whether the other person can give you a sense of security, or how you should respond?

reversed.overall: Upside down, the king on the sea still sits firmly, but that steadiness may turn into holding on by force: you look calm on the surface while pushing every emotion down, or you sometimes burst out suddenly. Someone may also wrap real feelings in reasonable-sounding words. This doesn't mean you're losing control. Your feelings need an outlet, and saying them somewhere safe will lighten the load a lot.
reversed.love: The other person may rarely express feelings, leaving you unable to tell what they're thinking. In a situationship they may always stay rational, go completely silent after losing contact, or you may keep swallowing things to avoid a fight. If you want to get back together, don't rely on logic alone. Pick an unhurried moment and share one feeling, without blame, such as "This made me a little sad."
reversed.work: You may have been the calm one for a long time and built up a lot of pressure, or your manager's moods may be hard to predict. Talk with someone you trust, or write your thoughts out, then decide what to say in the meeting. When your stress has somewhere to go, your judgment gets clearer.
reversed.ask_next: What you've been holding back: is it your dissatisfaction with them, or the demands you place on yourself?

upright.overall: A hand reaches out of a cloud holding a wooden staff sprouting new leaves, with a castle on a distant hill. The card shows a new passion or idea just emerging, with the power of a spark. It's a good time to grab it and take a first real step instead of leaving it in your head. The start doesn't need to be perfect. Just get moving.
upright.love: This is new attraction, or heat returning to a relationship. If you're in a situationship, you can take the lead and invite them to something you both enjoy. If you're out of contact or want to reconcile, this energy is worth using to make a fresh start. If you're together, try a new activity side by side. When the warmth comes, let the other person feel it.
upright.work: Good for starting a new project, pitching a new idea, or beginning a job search. Turn your idea into a simple action list and pick the first step to do right away, such as sending an email or updating your résumé, so enthusiasm becomes progress. The sooner you act, the less likely the enthusiasm is to cool.
upright.ask_next: What do you want to begin: a new relationship, or a new project?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the staff with new shoots is still in your hand, but the spark hasn't caught. You may want to do many things and not know where to start, or the timing may not be right yet, or your enthusiasm may come fast and fade fast. The card reminds you to find the one thing you want most. The tinder is still there. It just needs a clear direction.
reversed.love: Both of you may like each other but neither steps forward first, or things started hot and slowly cooled. After losing contact you may want to reach out but lack the energy, and the thought of reconciling comes and goes. If you're together, the spark may be missing. First ask yourself whether you like this person or just like being pursued, then decide whether to suggest meeting up.
reversed.work: A plan may be stuck at the starting stage, or you may be trying to do too much at once and spreading your energy thin. Cut your list down to the single most important thing and give yourself a small goal, such as finishing the outline of a proposal. Finish one thing and your motivation will come back on its own.
reversed.ask_next: Why haven't you started: because you haven't thought it through, or because you're afraid of failing?

reversed: Fear of leaving your comfort zone

upright.overall: A figure stands on a castle wall, a small globe in the right hand and a staff in the left, another staff fixed beside them, looking out over the sea and land. The card says you already have some foundation and are thinking about where to go next. It's a good time to plan carefully and choose a direction. You already hold some chips. Now it's time to decide how to use them.
upright.love: You may be wondering whether to take this relationship a step forward, or weighing two options: whether to make things clear in a situationship, whether to reach out after losing contact, whether to talk about getting back together, or whether to discuss longer-term plans once you're together. Write down the relationship you hope for, compare it with how things are now, and sort out what you can discuss and what you won't give up.
upright.work: Good for planning your career direction, considering an overseas assignment, or switching fields. Do your homework first, for example by checking the job requirements in your target industry or talking with someone already on that path, so your choice rests on information and not just imagination. A bit more information means a bit less hesitation.
upright.ask_next: What are you deciding now: whether to go, or which way to go?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the figure still stands on the wall holding the globe, but has looked for a long time without taking a step. Your current spot may be so comfortable that you hate to leave, or you may have thought everything through so thoroughly that you can't decide. The card reminds you that a plan has to land at some point. A small step is more practical than waiting until it's perfect.
reversed.love: You may keep wondering whether to speak plainly, or the other person's signals may make you hesitate to move forward. After losing contact, a message sits drafted and unsent, and the words about reconciling stay in your heart. If you're together, you may be afraid to talk about the future. Ask them one light question about the future, see how they answer, then decide your next step.
reversed.work: You may know you want a new job but keep stopping at browsing listings without applying. Pick the three best-fitting openings and apply, without waiting for a perfect résumé. Once you get real responses, you'll know more clearly what you want, and your next step won't be just imagination.
reversed.ask_next: What's holding you back: uncertainty about the future, or reluctance to leave the present?

upright.overall: A figure stands high up with their back to us, three staffs beside them, one held in hand, watching ships sail on the sea. The card shows that you've already sent something out and are now watching it travel and waiting for a reply. You can look further ahead. Things are growing into a wider scope, and what you need is patience and a steady gaze toward the distance.
upright.love: You may have already shown how you feel and be waiting for a reply from someone in a situationship. If you're waiting to hear from an ex, it's like sending your words out and waiting for the ship to return. In a long-distance or committed relationship, you need more patience. In the meantime, take care of your own life and share news now and then, so contact continues naturally without constant prodding.
upright.work: Good for expanding business, working across departments, or moving to another place. After sending your résumé or proposal, prepare your next step at the same time, such as questions you want to ask in an interview, so the waiting time keeps moving forward. Building one skill meanwhile will leave you more confident when the next chance comes.
upright.ask_next: What are you waiting for: the other person's response, or a signal you can feel at ease about?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the person watching the sea is still there, but the ships seem slower than expected, or they're sailing a different course than you pictured. A reply may be late, or a plan may be running into real-world limits. The opportunity hasn't vanished. What's needed is to check your expectations against where things actually stand. Once you adjust, the ship can keep moving forward.
reversed.love: Messages get answered slowly, or the relationship moves slower than you hoped. After no contact, you may be waiting on a reply; a reconciliation may stall halfway; or you may be together but feel you're on different paces. Instead of just waiting, get clear on what you expect from this relationship, then ask what they're thinking now, directly and gently. A real answer is more reassuring than guessing.
reversed.work: A project may be stuck at one step, or you may have heard nothing about a job application. Send a short note asking about progress, and at the same time check your plan for anything you missed. Adjust the goal if you need to, without giving up on it entirely. A revised plan often holds up better.
reversed.ask_next: What needs adjusting: your expectations, or your approach?

upright.overall: Four wooden staves stand in front, hung with garlands. Behind them two people raise bouquets high, and a castle sits in the distance. This card is about a stage finished well, worth pausing to celebrate. It also stands for stability and belonging, like returning to a place that puts you at ease, where you can catch your breath and share the joy with those around you.
upright.love: The relationship settles into a more secure place. A situationship may become something definite, two people who had lost contact or reconciled may find their rhythm again, and a couple may start meeting each other's friends or family. Plan a small celebration, such as a meal together, to mark how far you've come and let each other know this relationship is worth treasuring.
upright.work: A project may wrap up, you may pass a probation period, or your team may have results to show. Find a chance to celebrate with your colleagues, and write up what you learned so the next stage starts on firmer ground. Feeling recognized can become fuel to keep going.
upright.ask_next: Do you want to know whether this stability can last, or what the next step should be?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the garlands still hang on the staves, but the celebration seems postponed, or the mood isn't as light. You may be in a transition like moving or changing environments, or some foundation may not be set yet. The good news is only a little late. Settle what needs settling first, and your mind will settle with it.
reversed.love: The relationship may not yet have the approval of people around you, or the two of you may see the next step differently. A situationship may be slow to define itself, contact may have just resumed after a break, or you may not have regained a sense of safety after reconciling. Talk about what "stable" means to each of you, and build understanding from small things, like regular time together, rather than taking a big leap.
reversed.work: The team atmosphere may feel unsettled, or your results may not yet be formally recognized. Finish what's in your hands, put together concrete results, and bring them up with your manager at a good moment. You can also hold a small celebration with colleagues to acknowledge everyone's effort.
reversed.ask_next: What matters more to you: how others see it, or whether the two of you feel it's stable?

upright.overall: Five young people each hold a staff, swinging and sparring, like a contest with no winner yet. This card describes a stage where things are stuck on differing opinions and everyone talks past each other. Everyone has ideas, but the directions haven't lined up. Once it's out in the open, you learn what each person cares about. Lay out the differences and find where you can give a little.
upright.love: You may argue over small things lately, or in a situationship both sides may be testing and neither wants to give way first. If you're separated and hoping to talk again, you may slide back into old problems the moment you speak. For a couple, bickering can be a way of checking that you care. This doesn't mean you're incompatible. You're still working it out. Pick the one thing that matters most and talk it through, rather than unloading every complaint at once.
upright.work: You may face coworkers competing for resources, a meeting full of opinions, or plenty of other applicants. Putting your energy into making your proposal clearer works better than trying to beat someone. Write your argument in three points and follow them in the meeting. Healthy competition can bring out better work, and not every rival has to be an enemy.
upright.ask_next: Do you want to understand what the other person thinks, or what exactly you're arguing about?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the melee becomes tension beneath the surface: on the outside the arguing has stopped, but the disagreements are still there.
