Or you may want to avoid conflict so much that you swallow what needs saying, and grow more tired. The problem hasn't gone away, only been pressed down. Admit the conflict exists, then look together for an approach both sides can accept.
reversed.love: This may look like a cold war, messages left on read, or two people pretending nothing is wrong. In a break, neither wants to bend first; if you want to reconcile, you may fear another fight the moment you speak; and in a situationship, someone may be bottling up their dissatisfaction. Keeping quiet only widens the distance. Start with one small thing, like "I was actually a little bothered by what happened last time."
reversed.work: The team may seem harmonious on the surface while everyone works separately, or you may keep giving way so you won't upset anyone. That kind of friction drains energy. Write down roles and deadlines, using words instead of guesswork. If the conflict is already affecting progress, asking your manager to help sort it out is also an option.
reversed.ask_next: Right now, do you want to clear the air, or first figure out your own limits?

upright.overall: A rider on a white horse wears a laurel wreath, and the staff in hand is bound with a garland. People around raise their staves and follow. This card speaks of a stage where effort is seen and recognized. Your work is starting to get a response, and you can accept this acknowledgment steadily. There's no need to be overly modest, and don't ease off after one success. Keep the good rhythm going.
upright.love: The other person may start showing their affection openly, and a situationship may get a clearer response than before. If you've been out of contact and want to win someone back, you may sense their attitude warming. A couple may find friends are supportive of them. Accept this goodwill graciously and say what you feel, without pretending to be cool.
upright.work: A good time to seek visibility: a proposal gets adopted, your manager mentions your performance, or you get a promising reply. Turn what you've accomplished into concrete numbers and share them proactively on the right occasion. If you're waiting on an offer, read the terms carefully before you reply.
upright.ask_next: Are you trying to find out how the other person sees you, or whether you want to take one more step forward yourself?

reversed.overall: Upside down, the rider's wreath looks like it hasn't been set firmly on his head. You've done a lot, but the applause is slow to come, or you care so much about others' opinions that you start doubting yourself. The recognition is only running late. Rather than wait for someone to applaud you, acknowledge every step you've taken first, and others' responses will come in time.
reversed.love: You may feel your effort goes unseen, or keep waiting for the other person to speak up or go public first. After losing contact, you might wait for them to message first; you may want to get back together but fear coming on too strong; and if you're together, you may want a bit more affirmation. First ask yourself whether you're happy in this relationship, then pick a moment to ask directly how they see the two of you.
reversed.work: Credit may be getting shared out, your results may go unmentioned, or you may hear nothing for a long time after an interview. Don't rush to doubt yourself. Write down your results, find a good moment to set up time with your manager, and talk about your contribution and next steps. You can also use this gap to think about which of your abilities you most want recognized.
reversed.ask_next: Do you care more about others' recognition, or about how you see yourself?

upright.overall: One person stands on high ground, a wooden staff in hand, holding off six staffs reaching up from below. The two shoes don't match, as if they were pulled on in a rush to fight. The Seven of Wands shows you defending a position or an idea, with pressure coming from all sides, though where you stand is actually an advantage. You don't need to beat everyone. Just hold the one thing you truly care about.
upright.love: You may be speaking up for this relationship in the face of family and friends' opinions; holding your boundaries in a situationship; or refusing to give any more ground in the tug-of-war of lost contact or getting back together. First work out whether you're defending this person or just your pride, then say it gently but clearly. If you're together, let the other person know you're on the same side.
upright.work: You may need to defend your proposal, or face doubts in a new role. You have a position and reasons for it, so don't back down too fast. Get your data and grounds ready, and when answering doubts, stick to the issue, confident but not aggressive, and people will be more willing to trust you.
upright.ask_next: What you're defending right now: is it the relationship itself, or your own principles?

reversed.overall: Upside down, the person on high ground is struggling to hold on. It's not that the opponents are too strong, but that there is too much, and too mixed, to fend off. You may also be so defensive that you treat words that aren't attacks as attacks. Pick the one or two things truly worth defending and set the rest down for now. Leaving some battles isn't giving in; it saves your energy for where it matters more.
reversed.love: You may often feel you have to justify yourself, bristling at a single remark; in a situationship you take jokes as provocation, when lost contact or talking about getting back together you get guarded the moment you speak, and if you're together you may keep fighting about the same thing. Next time, pause and ask yourself: is this person criticizing, or telling me what they need? Then decide how to reply.
reversed.work: You may be pulled by too many people and chased by too many tasks. List what's on your plate and sort out what you must hold firm on and what can be handed off or postponed, saving your energy for what's important. Learning to choose your battles protects your professional image better than toughing out everything.
reversed.ask_next: Are you tired because the other person is really pushing you, or because you want to defend everything?

upright.overall: There are no people in the picture, only eight wooden staffs flying slantwise across the sky, with open fields and a river below. This card says things are speeding up. What was stuck begins to loosen, and messages, replies, or opportunities may arrive one after another. In this stage, thinking too long can mean missing the moment. Reply first, set out first, and adjust as you go.
upright.love: Contact becomes frequent and conversation warm, and a situationship may heat up quickly. Someone you lost contact with may suddenly message you, and the topic of getting back together may come up. If you're together, there may be plans for a trip or a next step. When things move fast, check in with your own feelings too. Reply sincerely, but there's no need to settle everything at once.
upright.work: You may receive replies, interview invitations one after another, or a project may suddenly speed up, and reacting quickly matters. Get your résumé, portfolio, and common replies ready so you can handle news the moment it arrives. If you're negotiating a collaboration, your response speed also shapes the other side's impression of you.
upright.ask_next: Do you want to know whether the other person will respond, or whether you should make the first move?

reversed.overall: Upside down, the eight staffs look suspended in midair, and the rhythm of things is disrupted. Messages may go unanswered, plans keep changing, or you may be so hasty that you throw off your own pace. This doesn't mean it falls through, only that it hasn't landed yet. Rather than keep pushing, use the pause to fill in details, so you have more room to catch things when the rhythm returns.
reversed.love: Messages may be slow to be answered, agreed plans may be postponed again and again, or you may be sending too much, too fast. If you've lost contact, don't rush to read meaning into their silence. If you want to get back together, don't say everything at once. In a situationship or relationship, you may both simply be too busy. Resist the urge to keep messaging, and give you both some space to see the rhythm.
reversed.work: Processes may stall, replies slow down, or you may be pushing too many things at once and finishing each only halfway. Put your tasks in order, focus on one at a time, and follow up politely once on progress. You can also use the gap to polish your résumé or learn a new tool.
reversed.ask_next: The thing you're anxious to know: is it stuck on the other person, or stuck in the process?

upright.overall: A figure with a bandaged head leans on a wooden staff, with eight more staffs standing behind, eyes still watching their surroundings. The Nine of Wands means you've already come a long, hard way, and though you're tired, you've reached the last stretch. For now, hold on, and don't let old wounds become new baggage. You are more resilient than you think.
upright.love: You may have been hurt before and are being very careful this time, unwilling to lower your guard. In a situationship you want to move closer but pull back first; after no contact, or when talking about getting back together, you keep remembering the last time it hurt. Caution isn't wrong, but also look at what the person in front of you actually does. If you're together, saying your worries out loud brings you closer than quietly guarding yourself alone.
upright.work: A project may be entering its final sprint, or you may have held a hard position for a long time. Don't let go at the last moment. List the remaining steps clearly and finish them one by one, and say what support you need, so your manager knows how much you've been carrying and sees your value in this role.
upright.ask_next: Is your hesitation about the person in front of you, or about past experience?

reversed.overall: Upside down, the bandaged figure is a little unsteady. You may be exhausted to the limit, or have been on guard for so long that you push away even good things as they approach. This isn't weakness. It's a reminder to restore your strength. Pausing isn't giving up. After you rest and look again, you'll see more clearly whether this is worth continuing.
reversed.love: You may fear being hurt again so much that any bit of uncertainty from the other person makes you want to back off. In a situationship you push the person away first; after no contact you simply stop expecting anything. If you want to get back together, first check whether you miss this person or just don't want to be lonely. If you're together, tell your partner you need a little time, and try to tell which worries come from old wounds.
reversed.work: You may have been working overtime for a long while with too many responsibilities, and now want to drop everything. Take a real break where you can fully switch off, or talk with your manager about your workload. Get your strength back, then decide whether to change paths. Decisions made when tired are easy to regret, so wait until you're steadier before deciding whether to stay or go.
reversed.ask_next: Do you want to drop the thing itself, or are you just too tired and in need of rest?

upright.overall: A figure hugs ten wooden staffs, face almost hidden, struggling toward a house ahead. The Ten of Wands means you're carrying a lot of responsibility; the goal is near, and the burden has peaked. The work can be finished, but your method needs adjusting, and you don't have to carry it all yourself. You can almost see the finish line. What matters most now is redistributing the weight so you aren't crushed.
upright.love: You may be handling most things in the relationship and growing more tired. In a situationship you keep going along with the other person; after no contact you've made up too many excuses for them; when you want to get back together, you're used to shouldering the repair alone. If you're together, ask for specific help, such as "Could you take this one?", instead of quietly doing everything and then feeling resentful.
upright.work: You may have taken on too many projects, or you're used to taking everything on; results are nearly there, but your efficiency is dropping. Pick one or two things you can hand over or ask someone to help with, and talk with your manager about priorities so everyone knows your plate is full.
upright.ask_next: Of all these responsibilities, which one doesn't actually have to be carried by you alone?

reversed.overall: Upside down, the bundle of staffs may finally be set down. You may be starting to realize you carry too much, or you may know it's heavy and still refuse to let go. Putting some down isn't failure; it lets you go farther. Set down one or two first, catch your breath, lift your head and see the direction, then decide what to keep carrying and what to hand off.
reversed.love: You may want to hand some responsibility back to the other person, or catch your breath in a very tiring relationship. In a situationship you don't want to hold it up alone anymore; after no contact you don't want to be the one who reaches out again; when talking about getting back together you hope they'll put in effort too. First figure out whether you're tired of this person or of this way of relating, then say the one thing you'd like to adjust.
reversed.work: You may be starting to learn to refuse and hand things off, or considering a more reasonable role. Practice saying no on one small thing first and watch what happens; you'll find letting go isn't so scary. Write your handoff as a list and pass it on, so others can take over easily and you can rest easier.
reversed.ask_next: Is what you want to put down one particular thing, or the whole way of relating or working?

upright.overall: A young person stands in a desert, both hands holding a staff sprouting new leaves, looking at it intently. Their clothes bear salamander patterns, and pyramids stand far off. This card is about a new thought or opportunity that has just appeared: still small, but full of enthusiasm. It's a good time to explore, ask, and try. There's no need to rush for answers; start with one small thing.
upright.love: A new situationship may be starting, or the other person may send a message tinged with curiosity; someone you've lost contact with may greet you again with a new topic. Right now, being relaxed matters more than being serious. If you're together or newly reunited, try something you've never done together. Start with shared interests and slowly grow closer.
upright.work: You may hear about a new job opening or project, or want to learn a new skill. Gather information first, talk to people who've done it, and write your idea as a simple one-page plan. Also notice who around you brings news; at this stage, opportunities often come from a casual chat.
upright.ask_next: Is your enthusiasm for this about truly starting, or just taking a look first?

reversed.overall: Upside down, the sprouting staff is still in your hand; you just haven't decided what to do with it. You may have many ideas but haven't started any, or your enthusiasm comes fast and fades fast. This isn't a lack of opportunity. The idea is still brewing and needs some patience and a concrete first step; only by doing it will you know if it suits you.
reversed.love: The other person may run hot and cold, or you may feel unsure about this situationship. If someone reappears after no contact, or you want to get back together, first see whether it's a passing impulse or real intent. If you're together, the novelty may fade quickly. Watch for a while whether you both keep engaging, and don't judge from one or two warm chats.
reversed.work: A new plan may stay stuck at the idea stage, or something you just began may lose motivation after a few tries. Pick the smallest action, such as sending one email or signing up for one class, to get the idea moving. After one small step, look back and you'll see more clearly whether this direction is worth investing in.
reversed.ask_next: Are you stuck because you don't know where to start, or because you're not sure you want it?

upright.overall: A knight rides a horse with its front legs raised high, holding a wooden staff, with pyramids behind him, ready to go. This card says the power to act has arrived. What you want to do has momentum, so it suits setting out boldly, trying a new direction, even moving or traveling. This passion is precious. Just look clearly at where you're headed before you leave, so you don't circle back to where you started.
upright.love: The other person may be pursuing you eagerly, or you may feel like making the first move. Someone who went silent may suddenly come back warm, and thoughts of reconciling may arrive fast. If you're together, it's a good time to plan a short trip. Passion is charming, but see whether it lasts. Inviting them is fine; just watch the pace of their replies.
upright.work: A good time to switch fields, take a new challenge, or go after an opportunity. Your drive will be noticed. Before you go, confirm two or three key points, such as pay and job scope. You can also ask people in the industry first, so your drive goes where it counts.
upright.ask_next: Is the direction you want to rush toward somewhere you truly want to go, or are you just wanting to leave where you are now?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the horse with its front legs raised seems to have lost its way. The drive is still there, but it doesn't know where to go. You may be making mistakes by hurrying, or wanting to do this one moment and that the next. The energy itself is fine. It just needs reining in first. Putting your strength into one direction works better than dashing off in all directions.
reversed.love: Their heat may come fast and fade fast, or you may send a message on impulse. In a flirtation you may push things too quickly. After going silent, you may reach for an ex on a whim without having thought through whether you want to reconcile. If you're together, words may come out too fast during an argument. Let your feelings cool first, save the message as a draft, and decide later whether to send it.
reversed.work: You may feel an impulse to quit, keep changing direction, or push a project so fast that things get missed. Before deciding, write down your reasons for wanting to go. Once the emotion passes, read them again to see whether it's a direction problem or just a passing mood. Drive in the right place is an asset. Settle the direction first, then set out.
reversed.ask_next: Will the decision you want to make now still feel the same once your emotions settle?

upright.overall: The Queen sits on a throne carved with lions, holding a wooden staff in one hand and a sunflower in the other, with a black cat at her feet. The Queen of Wands shows that you can manage your life well and have a warmth that draws people in. It suits trusting your own judgment and handling things with a cheerful, firm attitude. You don't need to please anyone. Put your passion into what you care about, and the people around you will naturally be moved by it.
upright.love: Your charm is at work. If you're in a flirtation, the other person is likely drawn to how at ease you are. If you want an ex to come back, living your own life well is more attractive than chasing them. If you're together, keep your own interests and circle of friends. Share what you love and let them see the real you.
upright.work: A good fit for a coordinating or leading role. Your enthusiasm can move the people around you. Offer ideas in meetings, or take on a task that shows your organizing skills, so others see how steady you are. Your presence is strong right now, which suits building trust and connections.
upright.ask_next: Are you trying to confirm how the other person feels, or whether you have confidence in yourself?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the sunflower in her hand seems to have put its light away for now. Lately you may have some self-doubt, or give so much to others that little is left for yourself, and your mood may swing more. Bring your attention back to yourself. Keeping a low profile for a while is fine. Once you take care of yourself, your passion and confidence will slowly return.
reversed.love: You may care too much about what the other person thinks and feel not good enough over small things. In a flirtation you may keep rechecking the tone of their messages. After going silent you may wonder if it was your fault, and feel unsure about reconciling. If you're together, you can say directly where you need care. Do one or two things that make you happy first, find your ease again, then face the relationship.
reversed.work: You may be looking after too many people and tasks at once, leaving yourself drained, or feel your ability isn't recognized. Do your own work well first, stop cleaning up after others, and save your energy for the tasks that really matter. Once your rhythm is steady, your ability will be seen again.
reversed.ask_next: Is your recent unease coming from the other person, or from what you demand of yourself?

upright.overall: The King sits on a throne holding a wooden staff that is sprouting, with lions and salamanders on the throne's back and a small salamander at his feet. The King of Wands says you have direction and the ability to carry things forward. It suits speaking up, making decisions, and owning the results. You don't have to wait for everyone to agree. State the direction clearly and things will move.
upright.love: You or the other person plays the leading role in the relationship. If you're in a flirtation, they may be waiting for you to give a clear direction. If you went silent and want to talk again, it helps for you to suggest a specific way to talk. If you're together, you can plan what comes next. Say what you think and expect, and ask for their views too, so leading doesn't become deciding alone.
upright.work: A good time to lead a project, negotiate terms, or go for a management role. Your vision can win people over. Organize your ideas into a clear direction and steps, and explain to the team why, so they're willing to follow. If you're considering a management role, you can evaluate it seriously now.
upright.ask_next: Do you want them to keep up with your pace, or the two of you to decide together?

reversed.overall: Reversed, the King still holds the sprouting staff, but he uses his authority a bit too hastily. You may want to control too much, or expect results too fast, and those around you can't keep up. Or you may not yet dare to state your views. The ability has always been there. Slow down and listen more, and more people will be willing to follow you.
reversed.love: One side may be too forceful, wanting everything done their way. In a flirtation you may push the other to commit. After going silent you may want one conversation to settle who wins, and when discussing reconciliation you may only state your own terms. If you're together and tend to decide for the other person, next time there's a disagreement, listen fully before replying, and replace "you should" with "how can we do this".
reversed.work: A manager may be too forceful, or you may be too eager for results and impatient with the team. State your expectations clearly and leave room for others to finish in their own way. Efficiency often improves. If you're the one being managed, you can speak up about the communication style you want.
reversed.ask_next: Do you want to change the other person's way of doing things, or the way you take the lead?

upright.overall: The card shows a hand reaching out of a cloud, gripping an upright sword with a crown at its tip. It speaks of seeing clearly: the key to the matter has surfaced, and you already have an answer in mind. This is a good time to say what you think and make a clear decision. Rather than keep circling, say the one sentence that matters most.
upright.love: This card gives you the strength to speak plainly. If things are ambiguous, you can ask the other person directly how they see the two of you. If you're out of contact or hoping to get back together, first work out what you want, then decide whether to reach out. If you're together, it's a good time to lay out what you've been talking around. Boil what you want to say down to a sentence or two, and get to the point when you message.
upright.work: At work, this is a good time to make decisions, propose plans, and negotiate terms. If your thinking is clear and your reasons hold up, you have a chance of being heard by your manager or the other side. Suggestion: before a meeting or interview, write your core argument in three sentences, then follow those three sentences as you speak and don't let other topics pull you off course.
upright.ask_next: You already have an answer in mind. Are you just waiting for the right moment to say it out loud?

reversed.overall: The hand from the cloud and the crowned sword are both still there, but the whole card is flipped and the sword points down. Reversed, it means your thoughts haven't settled yet, or you spoke too fast and too harshly and weakened your own position. The clarity hasn't gone away; it's just covered by noise for now. Work out which point you truly care about first, and you'll act with more strength.
reversed.love: You may have rehearsed many versions of the conversation in your head without saying any of them, or you spoke too sharply and the other person stepped back. People in ambiguous situations or out of contact often get stuck on the first; people hoping to reconnect or already together more often run into the second. Separate your feelings from the facts, and talk about just one thing at a time.
reversed.work: Your judgment is easily pulled around by too much information, or you came across too sharply in a meeting, so a good idea wasn't accepted. Suggestion: don't settle important decisions on the spot. Tell the other person you need time to think it through and will get back to them. Pick out the one point you really need to hold on to, and be willing to give way on the other details.
reversed.ask_next: What keeps you from deciding: not enough information, or fear of what will happen once you say it?

upright.overall: A woman sits blindfolded by the sea, arms crossed over her chest, a sword in each hand, with a crescent moon in the sky. This card is about not choosing yet: you have reasons on both sides, so you seal yourself off and keep up a calm surface. The standoff lets you catch your breath, but with a blindfold on you can't see the whole picture. Sooner or later you'll need to take the cloth off and look at what is in front of you.
upright.love: You and the other person may both be waiting for the other to speak first, leaving the relationship stuck in between. If things are ambiguous, you're guessing at feelings; if you're out of contact or hoping to reconnect, you're guessing who should reach out first; if you're together, you may keep steering around a certain topic. Rather than keep guessing, ask yourself what matters most to you, and once you know, take the initiative and ask once.
upright.work: Two options sit in front of you, like two job offers or two project directions, and you don't want to decide because you're afraid of choosing wrong. Suggestion: write the terms of both on the same sheet of paper, ask directly about any missing information, and don't rely only on how you feel in the moment.
upright.ask_next: You keep putting off choosing: are the two sides really about equal, or is there one you don't want to face?

reversed.overall: The blindfolded woman and the crossed swords are both flipped upside down. Reversed, it means the standoff can't be held much longer: information you've been avoiding is slowly coming to light, or you're simply tired and no longer want to pretend nothing is wrong. You don't need to solve everything at once, but you can first admit that part of you already leans toward one side.
reversed.love: Things that have gone unsaid are starting to come up, either because the other person asked first or because you couldn't hold back any longer. Those in ambiguous situations may be asked, "What are we?" Those out of contact or hoping to reconnect may meet the topic they never finished talking about. Those who are together may find small accumulated things rising to the surface. Hear the other person out fully first, then calmly say how you feel.
reversed.work: A choice you've been putting off is being pushed in front of you, and your manager or partner is waiting for your reply. Suggestion: even if you haven't decided, give a provisional answer, explaining what information you still need and how you plan to evaluate it. That will reassure them more than staying silent.
reversed.ask_next: If you had to choose right now, which side would your first instinct pick?

upright.overall: A red heart is pierced by three swords, with thick gray clouds and slanting rain behind it. This card speaks of sadness: a certain remark or outcome has left a sting in your heart. It doesn't mean things end here; it acknowledges that this hurt you. Allowing yourself to be sad for a while helps you move forward more than pretending nothing is wrong.
upright.love: Something has been said outright, or you heard an answer you didn't want. If things are ambiguous, you may find your hopes didn't pan out. If you're out of contact or hoping to reconnect, you may hear what the other person really thinks. If you're together, a single remark may have stung. Don't rush to send more messages asking for answers. Tell a trusted friend how you feel, and decide your next step once the emotion has passed.
upright.work: You may have been turned down, criticized, or worked hard for a long time without being noticed. That sense of loss is real, but it doesn't mean you aren't capable. Suggestion: pick out the genuinely useful parts of the feedback and write them down, set the rest aside for now, and don't let one setback define you.
upright.ask_next: What hurts most: the event itself, or your disappointment in yourself?

reversed.overall: The pierced heart and the rain clouds behind it are flipped upside down. Reversed, it means the wound is slowly healing, or that you've pushed the sadness down and never really dealt with it. Both say the same thing: this pain needs to be seen. You can let go bit by bit, without forcing yourself to be fine right away or pretending you stopped caring long ago.
reversed.love: You may still be thinking about a past relationship, or you've kept hurt feelings hidden and never told your partner. If you're out of contact or hoping to reconnect, it's easy to take out old wounds and look at them again and again. If things are ambiguous, past hurt may keep you from getting close again. Write down what you haven't said. You don't have to send it; just see clearly which sentence is holding you back.
reversed.work: Earlier setbacks are still with you, making it hard to work freely, and you hold back when giving opinions. Suggestion: pick one small task you're sure you can finish and complete it first. Let concrete progress bring your confidence back slowly. There's no need to prove anything to anyone; just find your own pace again.
reversed.ask_next: About the thing that hurt you: right now, do you want answers, or do you want to let go?

upright.overall: A knight lies flat on a stone slab in a church, hands pressed together in prayer. Three swords hang on the wall, and one more is carved on the side of the slab. This card says "stop for now." It isn't giving up. It's letting yourself catch your breath. Things won't run away because you rested, and once you quiet down, you'll see more clearly where to go next.
upright.love: This is a time to let the relationship breathe, not to push it forward. If things are undefined or you're out of contact, there's no rush to break the silence. If you want to get back together, a little distance helps you see more clearly. If you're together, talk less about problems and rest together more. Check their updates and online status less for now, and put your attention back on your own life.
upright.work: You may already be tired, or a project may be in a waiting-for-replies phase, and pushing hard won't do much now. Suggestion: turn what's on your plate into a list, set aside a stretch of rest where you truly don't touch work, and when you return, handle things one by one in order of priority.
upright.ask_next: Right now, do you need an answer, or do you first need to give yourself a good rest?

reversed.overall: The knight on the slab and the swords on the wall are all turned upside down when reversed. Reversed can mean you've rested enough and want to get back in the game. It can also mean you're very tired but can't stop, and your mind keeps spinning. See which one is you. In the first case, you can ease back into motion. In the second, treat rest as a real task to schedule, not something you do only when you have free time.
reversed.love: You may want to reach out to them again, or you keep thinking about the relationship so much that you can't sleep. If you're out of contact or want to get back together, first check whether you've truly made up your mind or you just don't want to wait anymore. If things are undefined or you're together, don't force an answer out of restlessness. Once you're clear, a simple, pressure-free message is enough.
reversed.work: The rest period is nearly over, and you want to dive back in, or your body is resting while your mind won't stop. Suggestion: warm up with one small task, such as answering an email or sorting files. Don't pack your schedule full the moment you're back at your post. Give yourself some buffer.
reversed.ask_next: Have you really rested enough, or do you just not want to stay where you are any longer?

upright.overall: A man holds three swords and looks back at two people walking away with their heads down, while two more swords lie scattered on the ground. This card shows the scene after a conflict: someone won, but the mood has soured. It asks you to think about what this fight was really about and whether it was worth it. Sometimes you win the argument but lose a relationship or a bit of trust.
upright.love: You may have just had a fight, or you keep comparing who feels more wronged. If you're together or want to get back together, you often get stuck waiting for the other person to admit fault first. If things are undefined or you're out of contact, you may be competing over who stays silent longer. Ask yourself whether you want to win or want the two of you to get along. If it's the latter, soften with one sentence first and give the other person a way to step down.
upright.work: There's a power struggle or competition at work, perhaps over credit, resources, or neither side giving way in meetings. Suggestion: where you need to argue your case, let data and facts speak, and don't try to win on emotion. Don't damage a relationship you'll still need for future collaboration over a momentary win.
upright.ask_next: In this dispute, what do you most want to win back?

reversed.overall: The swords on the ground haven't all been picked up and the heat of the fight lingers, but someone is starting to want to stop. Reversed means you or the other person wants to stop the tug-of-war and is willing to step back. It can also mean regret is left over after the fight. This is a good time to tidy things up. Nobody has to lose completely. If someone lowers their stance a little first, the conversation can start again.
reversed.love: After a fight or a cold war, someone wants to make up but can't swallow their pride. If you're together, start with a caring message that carries no blame. If you're out of contact or want to get back together, begin by asking how they've been, and don't rush to bring up old grievances. If things are undefined and there was some friction, use a light topic to reconnect. Take up old issues one at a time once the mood has eased.
reversed.work: The earlier conflict has a chance to dissolve, or you've realized that clashing head-on isn't worth it. Suggestion: talk to them privately. First say that you understand their position and pressures, then discuss how to divide the work going forward. This helps far more than staying locked in a standoff in front of everyone in a meeting.
reversed.ask_next: If you're the one to step back first, what are you most afraid of losing?

reversed: Can't let go of the past

upright.overall: In a small boat sit a cloaked woman and a child, while a ferryman poles toward the far shore, with six swords standing upright in the boat. This card is about leaving a painful place. The water is rougher on one side of the boat and calmer ahead. You may not be fully through it yet, but you're moving in a better direction, and it's fine if it's slow.
upright.love: The relationship is in transition. It may be slowly moving from arguments toward calm, or you may be letting go of a relationship. If you're out of contact, this distance gives you room to sort yourself out. If you want to get back together, don't rush to look back and check what they think. If things are undefined or you're together, the relationship is moving toward steadier ground. Start with one thing that makes you feel a bit better.
upright.work: This is a good time to adjust your environment, such as changing departments, changing jobs, or changing how you work. Suggestion: before you leave, hand over your tasks clearly, and look up and build the qualifications your destination requires, so the step is steadier and leaves no loose ends that are hard to tie up.
upright.ask_next: What you want to leave: is it the environment, or the person you were back then?

reversed.overall: The little boat carrying six swords is still on the water, but the whole card is flipped. Reversed means you want to leave but can't, or you've gone but your heart stayed behind. The transition is stuck halfway. Some things haven't been let go, and boarding with too much baggage makes the boat heavy. First see clearly what you still can't release, then decide whether to take it with you.
reversed.love: You may want to let go but keep going back to look at their messages or updates. People who are out of contact or want to get back together are most prone to this cycle. For those whose relationship is undefined or who are together, it may be old patterns replaying. You don't have to force a clean break right away. Start with something small, like archiving the chat history.
reversed.work: Your plan for change has been postponed, or you've changed positions but still work the old way. Suggestion: write down the specific reasons you want to leave or change, work out whether the problem is the environment or the approach, and then decide your next step, so you don't end up just as stuck in a new place.
reversed.ask_next: What keeps making you look back: is it reluctance to let go, or words left unsaid?

upright.overall: A figure tiptoes away carrying five swords, glancing back at the camp behind, where two swords are still on the ground. This card is about everyone having their own agenda: someone hasn't said everything, and that could be the other person or you. It isn't telling you to doubt everything. It reminds you to look closely and ask clearly on important matters, rather than guess.
upright.love: Some things may be unspoken between you, or you may be holding back what you really think. People in a situational ambiguous stage may each have kept an exit open, people who are out of contact or hoping to reconnect may not have said their real reasons, and people in a relationship may be keeping something inside. Rather than guess in private, pick a calm moment for both of you and ask one specific question directly.
upright.work: At work, someone may be pursuing their own plans, and information may not be fully shared. Suggestion: put important commitments and divisions of work in writing, and confirm meeting conclusions again by email. This protects you and gets everyone on the same page, so there's less "he said, she said" later.
upright.ask_next: What feels hidden from you: the other person's thoughts, or the part you don't want to say yourself?

reversed.overall: The figure carrying five swords away from the camp is turned upside down when reversed. Reversed, what was hidden starts to come out, or you find that carrying things alone and taking detours doesn't work. It's time to go back to open communication. Putting your real thoughts on the table takes far less effort than dodging, and you're less likely to be misunderstood.
reversed.love: Things left unclear before may have a chance to come out. People in an ambiguous stage may hear the other's honest feelings, people who are out of contact or hoping to reconnect may get a chance to share the reasons they left unsaid, and people in a relationship can bring up hidden frustrations. Start with your own feelings and don't rush to decide who's right, so the conversation can keep going.
reversed.work: A plan or idea that was kept private comes to the surface, or you find that working alone is simply too tiring. Suggestion: proactively update your manager or teammates on your progress and difficulties. When people know what you're doing, it's easier to get support when you need it, and you don't have to carry everything yourself.
reversed.ask_next: If you said everything openly, what reaction from the other person would you fear most?

upright.overall: A woman is blindfolded, her upper body wrapped in cloth, with eight swords planted around her and a castle on high ground in the distance. This card is about feeling trapped: part of what holds you is outside circumstances, and part is how you think about yourself. Her feet aren't bound and the swords don't form a full circle, so the way out isn't completely blocked.
upright.love: You may feel that every move in this relationship is wrong, that speaking and staying silent both seem bad. People in an ambiguous stage fear that asking will end it, people who are out of contact or hoping to reconnect fear that reaching out will look too humble, and people in a relationship fear that opening their mouth will start a fight. Change "I can't" to "I actually can," and pick one small step you can take now, even if it's just replying to a message.
upright.work: At work you feel bound by rules, your manager, or the whole environment, as if nothing you do is right. Suggestion: split your limits into two columns, "truly can't change" and "I assumed I can't change." Pick one from the second column and try moving it, then see what happens.
upright.ask_next: What holds you: real conditions, or the voice in your head saying "I can't"?

reversed.overall: The blindfolded woman and the eight swords around her are turned upside down together when reversed. Reversed, you begin to notice there is a path where you thought there was none, or you may still be standing in place but no longer want to stay this way. Take your time. One small step outward will show you options you hadn't noticed.
reversed.love: You begin to see your place in this relationship clearly and no longer just wait passively for the other person to decide. People in an ambiguous stage dare to ask plainly, people who are out of contact or hoping to reconnect can tell whether they want the person or fear being alone, and people in a relationship start saying what they need. Use one plain sentence, without blame, to tell the other person how you'd like to be together.
reversed.work: A situation that was stuck loosens, and you see other ways or other chances. Suggestion: don't rush to overturn everything at once. Find one small change to try, such as talking to your manager about adjusting one part of your job, see how people respond, then decide whether to go further.
reversed.ask_next: You've seen the exit. What's missing now: courage, or a concrete plan?

upright.overall: A person sits up in bed at night, hands covering their face, with nine swords hanging across the dark wall behind. This card is about worry and overthinking: many feared things haven't happened yet but have already replayed in your mind many times. Things may not be as bad as you imagine, and what most needs care is you, who hasn't stopped to rest.
upright.love: You may keep replaying one sentence from the other person or one read-but-unanswered message, growing more uneasy the more you think. People in an ambiguous stage wonder if the other isn't interested, people who are out of contact or hoping to reconnect replay the last conversation in their heads, and people in a relationship worry that things have changed. Sort your worries into "definitely happening" and "what I'm guessing," and your mind will settle a bit.
upright.work: Work pressure makes it hard to relax. You worry about doing poorly or being blamed, and you're still thinking about it after hours. Suggestion: pick one worry you can handle right now and start on it, put the rest on a to-do list instead of piling them all in your head, so you can truly rest after work.
upright.ask_next: About the thing keeping you awake, what outcome do you fear most?

reversed.overall: The person sitting up at night and the nine swords on the wall are turned upside down when reversed. Reversed, anxiety is easing and you can keep a little distance from your worries, or it has been pressed inside too long and you need someone to talk to. Either way, you're moving forward: say it out loud and let the worry move out of your head.
reversed.love: You begin to notice that some of your unease is something you made up, or you're finally willing to talk about your worries. If you're together or hoping to reconnect, begin with "I worry that..." and share your feelings and needs. If you're in an ambiguous stage or out of contact, don't demand to know why they haven't replied. Saying it calmly once is more useful than testing repeatedly.
reversed.work: Work pressure begins to find an outlet, or you realize you've been draining yourself and going in circles. Suggestion: talk with your manager or a trusted coworker about where you're stuck. Once you say it, you'll often find someone can share the load or offer an approach you hadn't considered.
reversed.ask_next: What you need most right now: an answer, or someone who will hear you out?

upright.overall: A person lies face down on the ground by the water, with ten swords across their back. The sky is dark, yet a band of golden light shows on the far horizon. This card says "this is where it ends": something has run its course, and holding on longer won't make it better. It sounds heavy, but it also means the hardest part is behind you. The light on the horizon says you can stand up again and begin anew.
upright.love: A relationship, or a way of relating, has reached its end, and more tugging back and forth will only wear you both out. If you're no longer in contact or hoping to get back together, stop asking why over and over. If it's a situationship, you can admit it didn't lead anywhere this time. If you're together, this is a good time to stop the argument that keeps coming back. Ask a friend to have a meal with you, and save your energy for yourself.
upright.work: A project, a job, or a way of doing things has hit the limit of what you can keep up. Suggestion: instead of forcing it, close it out properly. Write down what you learned in this time, then think about where to go next. Updating your résumé is a fine place to start.
upright.ask_next: If this really has come to an end, what do you most want to keep for yourself?

reversed.overall: The person on the ground, the ten swords, and the light on the horizon all turn upside down when reversed. Reversed, it suggests the lowest point has passed and you are recovering bit by bit. It can also mean something should clearly be over, but you won't let go, and it keeps wearing you out. Work out which one it is, then give yourself room to start again, one step at a time.
reversed.love: You may be slowly walking out of a relationship, or still finding it hard to let go of something that has already ended. If you're no longer in contact or hoping to get back together, don't keep looking back for answers. If it's a situationship, there's no need to rush to prove you're fine. If you're together, you can let past arguments truly turn the page. Take care of your daily life first: eat well, sleep well, and your heart will catch up slowly.
reversed.work: A low point at work is passing, or you're still propping up something that should have been wrapped up long ago. Suggestion: honestly assess whether it's still worth your effort. If not, list the steps to close it out. If it is, start with the smallest, easiest step.
reversed.ask_next: Are you still waiting for it to get better, or have you already decided on your next step?

upright.overall: The Page of Swords stands on rolling high ground, holding the sword up with both hands, head turned to one side, with clouds and birds in the sky behind. This card says things are still at the stage of gathering information. You want to know the truth, your mind is quick, and you're not afraid to ask. Now is a good time to look and listen more, and to list your questions clearly. Don't rush to a conclusion yet.
upright.love: You may be watching how fast the other person replies and the tone they use. If it's a situationship or you've just met, you can ask one specific question in a relaxed way. If you're no longer in contact or hoping to get back together, find out where the other person is now instead of judging from memories alone. If you're together, turn curiosity into questions. And when you ask, really listen to the answer.
upright.work: Work is a good place to do your homework: look into what a new position involves, find out how your manager leads people, and bring up the doubts you have about a project. Your sharpness is a strength, but when you're new or just taking something over, keep your questions about the issue, not the person. Suggestion: write your questions as a list before you speak.
upright.ask_next: What is the key piece of information you're missing right now?

reversed.overall: The Page holding the sword high is turned upside down. The curiosity is still there, but it has turned into unease: overthinking, filling in the story from fragments you've heard, or speaking too fast and hurting someone without meaning to. The situation itself may not have changed; the information reaching you is just too mixed. Pause, and separate what is fact from what is guesswork. The next step will be easier.
reversed.love: One unanswered message can send your mind into several versions of the story. If it's a situationship or you're no longer in contact, don't ask friends all around or keep scrolling their profile. If you're hoping to get back together, don't treat hearsay as what the other person thinks. If you're together, don't say things too fast. If you really care, ask directly once, then give them a little time to respond.
reversed.work: You may hear a lot of gossip at work, such as the department being reorganized or your manager having issues with you. Don't pass it along, and don't rush to snap back or decide anything. Suggestion: confirm once, face to face, with the person in charge, and keep what you heard separate from what you've confirmed. You'll feel steadier.
reversed.ask_next: Is what's unsettling you something you've confirmed, or something you've heard?

upright.overall: The Knight of Swords rides a white horse at full speed, sword raised high, the trees behind him bent by the wind. This card marks a time when things move fast. You've thought it through and want to act right away. It affirms your decisiveness and drive, and reminds you that the faster you go, the more you need to check you're headed the right way, so you don't miss the warnings along the road.
upright.love: This is a time to say what needs saying. If a situationship has dragged on, you can speak up first. If you're no longer in contact or hoping to get back together, you may have the courage to reach out. If you're together, it's a good time to talk through what's been set aside and reach a conclusion. But being direct is not the same as pressing for answers: say how you feel first, then ask what they think, and stop there so they have room to respond.
upright.work: Work is good for a sprint: projects with clear goals and proposals that are time-sensitive can be pushed forward decisively. When negotiating an offer or changing jobs, your directness can leave a strong impression. Suggestion: write down your key points and your bottom line before you set out, so you don't go too far in the moment.
upright.ask_next: Are you in a hurry because you've thought it through, or because you don't want to wait anymore?

reversed.overall: The reversed Knight of Swords is still on the white horse and the drive is still there, but the direction has gone astray. You may be rushing decisions, speaking too harshly, or running in several directions at once and getting stuck everywhere. Let the horse stop and catch its breath. See the road clearly before you go on, and your energy will go to the right place. Speed itself isn't wrong; you just need to pick one road first.
reversed.love: One person may be pushing too hard for an answer, making the other want to step back. If it's a situationship, don't press them to define the relationship right now. If you're no longer in contact or hoping to get back together, don't send a long string of messages all at once. If you've just had a fight, wait until emotions settle before talking. Pick the one thing you most want to say and say it well. Leave the rest for next time.
reversed.work: At work it's easy to make mistakes by rushing, such as agreeing before reading the terms clearly, or clashing head-on with your manager in a meeting. Slow down a little, put what's in front of you in order, and push one thing at a time. Suggestion: have a trusted colleague read important replies before you send them.
reversed.ask_next: Is the thing you most want to rush at right now really the thing to do first?

upright.overall: The Queen of Swords sits sideways on her throne, her right hand holding an upright sword, her left hand reaching forward, as if inviting you in and drawing a line at the same time. This card is about seeing things with a clear head: you've been through some things and are no longer easily carried off by your emotions. It's a good time to say things plainly and state your boundaries, without swallowing what you really think just to keep the mood pleasant.
upright.love: You know clearly what you want and what you don't. In a situationship, you don't need to pretend you don't care. With someone you've lost contact with or want to get back together with, you can honestly say what your terms are. If you're together, it's a good time to state your boundaries rather than bend yourself to fit. Say the thing you care about directly, with a gentle tone and clear content.
upright.work: At work, your judgment and orderly thinking get noticed. It suits tasks that need calm analysis, or a talk with your manager to clarify who does what. You can also compare the terms of an offer rationally. Try organizing your needs into a few points and confirming them one by one when you talk.
upright.ask_next: The line you want to draw: does the other person know where it is?

reversed.overall: The Queen and her sword have turned upside down. The clarity is still there, but it has turned into defensiveness: your words may be too sharp, or your heart closed so tightly that even kindness is kept out. An old experience may also still be unresolved, making it hard to trust the person in front of you. Admitting what you're protecting is more useful than forcing yourself to stay calm. Clarity and softness can exist together.
reversed.love: Someone may be protecting themselves with coldness, caring but deliberately not replying. If it's a situationship, don't test the other person by blowing hot and cold. If you've lost contact or want to reconnect, don't let old hurts speak for you. If you're together, don't use sarcasm or the silent treatment in place of communication. Try saying one honest sentence, see how the other person receives it, then decide whether to say more.
reversed.work: At work you may speak so bluntly that colleagues feel criticized, or hold others to standards so strict that people are afraid to approach you. You can keep your standards and adjust how you express them; feedback only helps if people can take it in. Next time you give feedback, start with what the person did well, then raise the one thing to change.
reversed.ask_next: The wall you built: does it still need to be that high?

upright.overall: The King of Swords sits facing forward on his throne, a long sword in hand, his expression steady, butterflies carved into the back of the chair. This card stands for handling things with reason and principle: look at the facts, use logic, make clear decisions. When it's time to decide, you can judge calmly without being swayed by a passing mood, and you can draw on expert opinion to make your decision stand on firmer ground.
upright.love: This suits laying the relationship out on the table. Don't guess; say clearly what each of you expects. In a situationship, you can ask how the other person sees things. If you've lost contact or want to reconnect, first look back calmly at why you split. If you're together, put expectations into concrete terms, such as how often to meet, rather than only talking about feelings.
upright.work: At work, this suits making decisions, negotiating terms and setting rules. With managers or clients, speaking with data and facts is very persuasive. When considering a job change or an offer, list the terms and compare them. Where you need expert judgment, ask someone who knows.
upright.ask_next: With this matter, are you short on information, or do you already have an answer and just don't want to decide?

reversed.overall: The seated King of Swords is upside down. Reason is still there but overused: you may hold too stubbornly to your own logic and not hear others, or someone around you may use rules to press people down. You may also be thinking too much and putting off a decision. Loosen up a little and listen to one more different voice, and your judgment will come back into balance.
reversed.love: One person may always be arguing logic and sorting out right from wrong while overlooking the other's feelings. If you're together or want to reconnect, don't rush to prove you're right in an argument. If it's a situationship or you've lost contact, don't analyze the other person's silence into a neat conclusion. Pause and ask, "What do you need right now?" before you continue.
reversed.work: At work you may face a very forceful manager, or you may be managing your team too tightly. You can hold to your principles, but leave some room for others to contribute, or things won't move. At your next meeting, hear everyone's views first, then give your conclusion and reasons.
reversed.ask_next: Are you holding on to the reasoning itself, or to the feeling of not giving in?

upright.overall: A hand reaches out from the clouds, steadily holding up a coin, with a flowering garden and a hedge archway below. This card stands for a practical new beginning: the opportunity is already in front of you, something you can touch and build on. It's a good time to reach out and take it, lay a foundation in small ways, and grow it step by step, without thinking too far ahead at the start.
upright.love: This is a stable, grounded starting point. A situationship partner may be someone willing to show it through actions. If you've lost contact or want to reconnect, you can restart with an actual meeting rather than long talks from a distance. If you're together, it's a good time to plan everyday life things together. Start with a specific date or a small project for two.
upright.work: At work, a new offer, a new project, or a direction worth investing in may appear. This card values the practical: look at pay, growth and whether it can last. Before accepting an opportunity, write down the terms and check them against your long-term goals before you say yes.
upright.ask_next: This opportunity in your hands: what do you plan to do with it first?

reversed.overall: The hand in the clouds holding the coin is turned completely upside down when reversed. The opportunity is still there but hasn't landed: terms may not be settled, the plan may be stuck on paper, or you may still be hesitating over whether to take it. It needs a bit more careful planning to take shape. Ask yourself whether what's missing is resources, time, or a little confidence.
reversed.love: There may be a good beginning that hasn't moved to the next step. In a situationship, the other person may still be watching and waiting. If you've lost contact or want to reconnect, your thoughts may stay in your head without action. If you're together, agreed plans keep getting postponed. Don't keep testing the waters through messages; arrange one real meeting and see whether you both want to move forward.
reversed.work: At work, an offer may be delayed, a budget stuck, or a plan stalled. There's no need to drop everything. First do well the parts you control, so the plan can start at any moment. List which conditions are still missing and fill them in one by one; progress may be faster than you expect.
reversed.ask_next: You haven't taken hold of it yet: are the conditions not enough, or have you not made up your mind?

upright.overall: A person lightly tosses two coins, joined by a ribbon in the shape of an infinity symbol. Behind them, ships rise and fall on the waves. This card is about keeping your balance amid change: you have several things in your hands, and you're managing them reasonably well. The point is to adjust your pace and respond as things shift, not to do every one of them perfectly.
upright.love: You may be splitting your time between work, family, and love. If you're in a situationship, the other person may be busy too, replying fast one day and slow the next. If you're out of touch or hoping to get back together, changes in your lives make it hard to find the same rhythm. If you're together, learn to fit around each other. Don't judge their feelings only by how fast they reply. Set aside an unhurried stretch of time to talk properly.
upright.work: At work, you may be handling several projects at once, or running between a main job and a side job. You adapt well and can handle change, but watch your energy and focus. Rank what's on your plate, say no when you need to, and don't take everything on yourself.
upright.ask_next: Of the things you're holding right now, which one could you actually set down first?

reversed.overall: The person juggling coins and the rolling sea behind them are turned upside down in reverse: too much to do, too little time, and nothing gets proper attention. This isn't a question of ability. The load is simply too heavy. Right now it helps to admit you can't catch everything, put down one or two things, and bring your pace back to something you can control. Then you can catch what remains more steadily.
reversed.love: Being busy may have led you to neglect the other person, or they may be so busy that you feel unimportant. For a situationship, this can easily cool things off. If you're out of touch or hoping to get back together, think about whether this is where things got stuck before. If you're together, don't compete over who is busier. Share how things have been lately, and agree on a way of keeping in touch that works for both of you.
reversed.work: At work, schedules may clash and details may slip. Instead of pushing through alone, bring up priorities with your manager. Write down everything on your list, cross out what can wait or be handed off, and keep only what truly needs you.
reversed.ask_next: Is it that there's too much to do, or that you find it hard to say no?

upright.overall: A craftsman stands on a church bench carving an arch, while two people below hold plans and discuss them with him. This card stands for collaboration and expertise: each person takes the part they're good at, and together they do the job well. Your ability is being noticed. This is a good time to talk through your ideas and listen to others' views, which can make the work more complete and let more people see your value.
upright.love: A relationship doesn't run on feeling alone. It needs two people willing to talk things through and adjust together. If you're in a situationship, you can grow closer by doing something together. If you're out of touch or hoping to get back together, first talk about where you didn't work well together in the past. If you're together, planning something side by side suits you. Say what you each expect, and find an approach you both are willing to take.
upright.work: At work, your expertise is likely to be recognized. This suits team projects, working with other departments, or showing your portfolio in an interview. Your manager may start noticing your performance. Check in on progress with the people you work with, so everyone moves forward from the same plan.
upright.ask_next: In this matter, whose cooperation do you need most to be able to move forward?

reversed.overall: The craftsman carving the arch and the two people with the plans are turned upside down in reverse: the collaboration is still going, but coordination is stuck. People may want different things, communication may be thin, or your contribution may not be seen. No one is necessarily wrong. You just define "done well" differently. Sitting down to align on the goal matters more than working on your own, and it's less tiring too.
reversed.love: You may feel that you're the only one making an effort. If you're together, it's easy to quietly keep score. If you're in a situationship, you may notice you're always the one finding things to talk about. If you're out of touch or hoping to get back together, perhaps things got stuck on unequal give and take. Pick a calm moment and say specifically what you'd like the other person to share, rather than just "you don't care."
reversed.work: At work, you may run into unclear roles, coworkers each doing their own thing, or credit being overlooked. Rather than stew, turn your contributions into concrete results people can see. Set up a discussion to settle roles, timelines, and what counts as finished, all at once.
reversed.ask_next: Where you feel stuck, is it that you're heading in different directions, or that you haven't communicated enough?

upright.overall: A person sits hugging one coin tightly, with one coin on their head and two under their feet, a city behind them. This card is about holding on to what you already have: you value security and want to keep things steady in your hands. This caution has its reasons, but remember that if you hold on too tightly, you have no hand free for anything new.
upright.love: You may badly want the relationship to stay stable, or feel unsure about expressing yourself first. If you're in a situationship, holding back too much leaves the other person unable to read your feelings. If you're out of touch or hoping to get back together, you may still be clinging to how things used to be. If you're together, you have enough security and could use a little flow. Share one small thing you don't usually say, and give the other person a chance to come closer.
upright.work: At work, this is a time to hold your current position and build your strength. Facing a job change or a new offer, you'll be more conservative and want to see clearly first, and there's nothing wrong with that. List what you gain now and what it might cost you, then decide whether to move.
upright.ask_next: This thing you're gripping so tightly: is it something you truly need, or something you're afraid to lose?

reversed.overall: The person hugging the coin, turned upside down in reverse, can be read two ways. One is gripping even harder, so afraid of loss that you can't release anything. The other is that you've begun to loosen your hand and let some things flow. See which fits you better lately. Either way, the point is to find the feeling of "this is enough" again, stop being pushed by fear, and decide calmly what to keep and what to release.
reversed.love: One of you may be so anxious that you keep checking on where the other is, or you may finally be ready to loosen your hold on the past. If you're together, care can easily turn into watching. If you're in a situationship, you may want to seize every reply. If you're out of touch or hoping to get back together, you may be learning to let go. Write down what makes you uneasy, and tell apart what the other person causes from what you bring yourself.
reversed.work: At work, you may fear mistakes so much that you do everything yourself, or refuse to share resources. It may also be that you're ready to leave a job that makes you unhappy and want a different setting. Think through what the worst case would be if you let go. It's usually less frightening than imagined, and it makes deciding easier.
reversed.ask_next: If you loosened your grip a little, what are you most afraid would happen?

upright.overall: Two figures walk through heavy snow past a lit stained-glass window. They are thinly dressed, heads down, not looking in. This card speaks of a tight stretch: maybe resources are short, maybe you feel shut out. It also reminds you that warmth is close by, you just haven't looked up yet. This time will pass. For now, don't carry it alone.
upright.love: You may feel lonely, overlooked, or unable to get the response you want in a relationship. If you're out of contact or hoping to reconcile, it's easy to grow colder the more you think. If things are ambiguous, you may feel left outside. If you're together, the closeness you need may have gone unseen. Don't carry it alone. Talk with a friend you trust first, then think about whether to speak up.
upright.work: At work you may face tight income, a rough job search, or a sense of being pushed to the margins of your team. This is a stretch to get through, and it doesn't mean you aren't good enough. Try reaching out for help, such as asking a senior colleague to look over your résumé, or telling your manager what you're struggling with.
upright.ask_next: Is there a lit window near you that you haven't knocked on yet?

reversed.overall: In reversed, the snowy scene and the lit window turn over: you start to find a way out, you're willing to ask for help, or you finally see that someone is there. It may also be that you're still stuck on the thought of "I'll just handle it myself," and you push help away. Accepting support isn't weakness. It's the first step toward warming up, and the road gets easier bit by bit.
reversed.love: You may be slowly coming out of a relationship that went cold, or be willing to trust someone again. If you're out of contact and want to reach out or reconcile, start with a simple hello and don't press for answers. If things are ambiguous, try accepting the other person's kindness. If you're together, close the chilly distance a little at a time. Take care of yourself first, and move forward once you feel steady.
reversed.work: At work, the hardest part may be nearly over, and someone starts to lend a hand or a new direction appears. Don't turn down an opportunity just because things went badly before. Give yourself room to try. Say specifically what help you need so others know how to give it.
reversed.ask_next: How far away is the help you're willing to accept?

upright.overall: A well-dressed merchant holds a scale in one hand and hands out coins with the other to two people kneeling on the ground. This card is about how resources flow: some can give, some happen to need, and the scale reminds you that sharing should be fair. In this matter you may be the giver or the receiver. Neither position is lower. What matters is that both sides feel it is reasonable.
upright.love: This card looks at whether giving goes both ways. If things are ambiguous, a partner who responds and spends time on you is a good sign. If you're out of contact or hoping to reconcile, think about who gave more in the past. If you're together, notice who always does a little extra. Pick a relaxed moment to talk about each other's expectations, so both of you can give and also receive.
upright.work: At work, this card often points to how resources are shared: a raise, a bonus, a manager giving you a chance, or you mentoring a newcomer. When negotiating, bring concrete results and you're more likely to get a reasonable response. If you're the one giving, state clearly how far your help goes, so it doesn't become taken for granted.
upright.ask_next: In this matter, are you more the giver, or the one waiting for a hand?

reversed.overall: In reversed, the merchant, the scale, and the two kneeling people all turn over. The giving is still there, but it becomes uneven: one side may keep giving while the other gets used to receiving, or help may come with conditions that make it uncomfortable to accept. First look at the books honestly: where you give too much, where you feel awkward speaking up. Then slowly bring the balance back.
reversed.love: In love, you may be the one always messaging and arranging meetups while the other only responds, or the other person's kindness may feel like pressure. If you're out of contact or reconciling, consider whether someone was always filling the gaps before. Try pausing your own giving and see whether the other person takes a step forward.
reversed.work: At work, you may be doing a lot and getting little, or a manager's opportunity may carry unspoken conditions. When changing jobs or weighing an offer, get the terms in writing before you agree. If you often help colleagues finish their work, start practicing saying, "This time I'll focus on my own progress."
reversed.ask_next: Are you checking whether the other person gives enough, or whether you give too much?

upright.overall: A young farmer leans on his hoe, looking at coins growing on a vine. He has done a lot, and now he pauses to assess: is this field worth tending further? This card says things are still in their growing stage. Results have taken shape but aren't ready to harvest. It's a good time to take stock of what you've put in and what you've gotten back, then decide where to place your energy next.
upright.love: This relationship has some foundation but is still growing slowly. If things are ambiguous, the other person responds slowly but is building something. If you're out of contact or hoping to reconcile, look at what this distance has helped each of you grow. If you're together, review what you've built together lately. Don't rush for answers. Watch what the other person keeps doing.
upright.work: At work, you've put time into your current project or career direction, and results are starting to show but aren't ready to harvest. It's a good time for a midpoint review: what is working, and what is spinning its wheels. Write down your conclusions, then decide whether to push harder or change direction.
upright.ask_next: What do you most want to know right now: whether this is worth continuing, or how to adjust?

reversed.overall: In reversed, the farmer leaning on his hoe and the coins on the vine turn over, and patience has worn thin. You may have worked a long time without seeing results and begun to doubt yourself, or you may be so eager for results that you pull up what hasn't finished growing to check on it. Your effort isn't wasted. Your energy may just be going to the wrong place, or your expected pace differs from reality, and it's worth reallocating.
reversed.love: You may have waited a long time and the other person's response stays lukewarm. If things are ambiguous, you're getting tired. If you're out of contact or hoping to reconcile, you keep wondering whether to try once more. If you're together, you feel like you're the only one watering. Honestly tell apart whether you're waiting because the other person is truly drawing closer, or because you can't stand to stop, then decide whether to keep investing.
reversed.work: At work, a project may have dragged on without progress, or you may have worked in a role for years without being noticed. This is a good time to weigh your input against what you get back, and to talk with your manager about your direction. If there's still no room after that, changing direction is a reasonable choice.
reversed.ask_next: Do you truly see no results, or are you just tired and in need of a rest?

upright.overall: A craftsman sits at his workbench, carving coins one by one, with his finished pieces hung on the post beside him. This card is about focusing on doing one thing well: practicing a little at a time, finishing one piece after another. How this situation moves forward is directly tied to how carefully you put yourself into it. There are no shortcuts, but every step counts.
upright.love: This card is about tending things through action. If things are undefined, steady care and remembering the small things the other person said carry more weight than pretty words. If you're out of contact or want to get back together, first act on what you want to improve in yourself. If you're together, it's a good time to build daily habits as a couple. Pick one small, concrete thing and keep doing it, so the other person can see you mean it.
upright.work: At work, this is a good time to learn skills, polish your work, and strengthen the basics. In a new job or role, doing your own part solidly is more useful than rushing to impress. Pick one professional skill and set aside regular practice time, and let the results build up slowly.
upright.ask_next: Right now, do you need to practice a little more, or to let others see what you've made?

reversed.overall: The craftsman and his coins are upside down. He is still carving, but his heart is no longer in it. Maybe the same task has gone on so long that you only want to get it done. Or maybe you demand so much perfection that one coin gets reworked again and again and never gets handed over. Being earnest isn't wrong. Your method may just need a change, or you may need to rest first and then come back to the bench.
reversed.love: Time together may have turned into routine, with messages that are only check-ins. Or you may be worrying too much about whether every detail is good enough. If things are undefined, don't polish every sentence to perfection before you send it. If you're out of contact or want to get back together, don't keep repeating the same apology. If you're together, find something new that you both enjoy doing.
reversed.work: At work, this may mean burnout, learning nothing new, or standards so high they slow your progress. Start by listing which tasks are fine at 80 percent, and save your energy for what really matters. If the whole job drains your motivation, it may be time to think about your next step.
reversed.ask_next: What's holding you up: the task itself, or what you demand of yourself?

upright.overall: A woman stands in a garden heavy with grapes, a falcon perched on her gloved hand, looking calm. This card is about security you built on your own: you can take care of yourself, and you know how to enjoy what your hard work has earned.
